definition_zh: 结构的；结构性的；建筑承重构造的；系统深层的
definition_en: relating to the structure or framework of something, especially to its load-bearing parts or its underlying organization
core_image: 一座桥的钢架剖面被抽掉一块，周围的梁柱仍把重量一步步传向地基
scene: 这里指「结构的」。 The survey found structural damage beneath the bridge deck.
sceneCN: 这里 structural 是「结构上的、承重构造的」（第 2 个义项：与建筑的梁柱和承重体系有关）；句意：检测发现桥面下方存在结构损伤。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、桥墩、裂缝、承重箭头。

pos.zh: 结构的；结构性的；建筑承重构造的；系统深层的

senses.title: Relating to a framework
senses.definition: relating to the way the parts of something are arranged and connected to form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 与某物各部分如何排列、连接成一个整体的方式有关
senses.example: The essay compares the structural features of the two novels.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章比较了这两部小说的结构特征。
senses.why: Latin structura named a fitting together, from struere 'to build'; the adjective therefore points to arrangement rather than to surface appearance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 structura 指「拼合、建造」，出自 struere「建造」；因此这个形容词指向排列方式，而不是表面外观。

senses.title: Load-bearing parts of a building
senses.definition: relating to the beams, columns, walls and foundations that carry weight and keep a building standing
senses.definitionCN: 与承担重量、使建筑站立的梁、柱、墙与基础有关
senses.example: A structural engineer approved the plans before construction began.
senses.exampleCN: 施工开始前，结构工程师批准了图纸。
senses.why: This engineering sense is the concrete core of the metaphor: the parts that bear load are literally the structure, and damage to them threatens the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这一工程义项是比喻的具体核心：承重的部件就是字面意义上的结构，它们的损伤会威胁整体。

senses.title: Of a language as a system
senses.titleCN: 语言学中的结构：把语言视为系统
senses.definition: in linguistics, describing language as a system of relations among sounds, words and sentences rather than as a list of items
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，把语言描述为声音、词与句子之间的关系系统，而不是一份条目清单
senses.example: Structural analysis shows that the two dialects share the same sound system.
senses.exampleCN: 结构分析显示，这两种方言共享同一套语音系统。
senses.why: Twentieth-century linguistics shifted attention from isolated words to the network that holds them together, and structural became the label for that viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪语言学把关注点从孤立的词转向维系它们的网络，structural 成为这一视角的标签。

senses.title: Underlying causes in a system
senses.definition: describing a cause that lies in the organization of a system rather than in the choices of one person
senses.definitionCN: 指某项原因存在于系统的组织方式中，而不是某个人的选择中
senses.example: Poverty in the region is structural, not a matter of individual effort.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的贫困是结构性的，与个人努力无关。
senses.why: If the arrangement of institutions produces the outcome, blaming individuals misses the mechanism; structural names that mechanism and is often opposed to personal or accidental.
senses.whyCN: 如果制度安排产生了这一结果，归咎个人就错失了机制；structural 命名这一机制，常与「个人的」「偶然的」相对。

senses.title: Change that alters the framework
senses.titleCN: 改变框架本身的结构性变革
senses.definition: describing reform or change that alters the basic organization of an economy, industry or institution rather than adjusting its surface
senses.definitionCN: 指改变经济、产业或机构基本组织方式的改革，而不是表面调整
senses.example: The country undertook structural reforms in taxation and labour law.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在税制与劳动法方面进行了结构性改革。
senses.why: Policy language distinguishes a structural reform from a temporary fix: the former changes the rules that generate outcomes, not just the outcomes themselves.
senses.whyCN: 政策语言把结构性改革与临时补救区分开：前者改变产生结果的规则，而不只是结果本身。

senses.title: Arrangement of molecules or cells
senses.titleCN: 分子或细胞层面的结构
senses.definition: in chemistry and biology, relating to the arrangement of atoms, molecules or tissues and how that arrangement determines function
senses.definitionCN: 在化学与生物学中，与原子、分子或组织的排列方式以及该排列如何决定功能有关
senses.example: Structural biology revealed how the protein binds its target.
senses.exampleCN: 结构生物学揭示了这种蛋白质如何结合靶点。
senses.why: Function follows form at the molecular scale: knowing how the parts are arranged explains what the molecule can do, which is why the adjective attaches to biology.
senses.whyCN: 在分子尺度上功能随形式而来：了解各部分如何排列，就能解释分子能做什么，因此这个形容词常与生物学搭配。

senses.title: Inequality built into society
senses.titleCN: 制度化的结构性不平等
senses.definition: describing disadvantage that is reproduced by the rules, norms and organization of a society rather than by individual prejudice alone
senses.definitionCN: 指由社会的规则、规范与组织方式不断再生产出来的不利处境，而非仅由个人偏见造成
senses.example: The report documented structural inequality in housing and schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了指住房与教育方面的结构性不平等。
senses.why: This social sense extends the engineering image to institutions: the rules act as beams that distribute advantage unevenly, so the pattern persists even when individuals change.
senses.whyCN: 这一社会义项把工程意象扩展到制度：规则像梁一样不均匀地分配优势，因此即使个人更替，模式仍然持续。

senses.title: Damage to the load-bearing frame
senses.definition: describing physical damage that affects the frame or foundation of a building, vehicle or machine rather than its surface
senses.definitionCN: 指影响建筑、车辆或机器框架或基础的物理损伤，而不是表面损伤
senses.example: The earthquake caused structural damage but no injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 地震造成了结构损伤，但无人受伤。
senses.why: This sense returns to the literal core: cosmetic cracks can be repaired, but structural damage means the part that carries the load is compromised, so the whole is at risk.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项回到字面核心：表面裂缝可以修补，而结构损伤意味着承重部件受损，整体因而处于风险中。

intro.en: Structural is structure plus the adjective ending -al; structure comes from Latin structura 'a building, a fitting together', from struere 'to build, pile up'. The deeper root is reconstructed.
intro.cn: structural 是 structure 加形容词词尾 -al；structure 出自拉丁 structura「建筑、拼合」，源自 struere「建造、堆叠」。其更深词根为重构形式。

items.en: Latin struere meant 'to build, pile up, arrange', and its past participle structus supplied the notion of something already built. The deeper root is reconstructed as Indo-European *streu- 'to spread, pile up'.
items.cn: 拉丁 struere 意为「建造、堆叠、安排」，其过去分词 structus 提供「已建成之物」的概念。更深词根被重构为印欧语 *streu-「铺开、堆积」。

items.en: Structura named the act of building and the building itself, hence 'a fitting together, an arrangement'. It is the direct source of English structure.
items.cn: structura 指建造行为及建筑物本身，因而表示「拼合、安排」。它是英语 structure 的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed structure in the fifteenth century, first for buildings and later for the arrangement of any organized whole.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 structure，最初指建筑物，后来指任何有组织整体的排列方式。

items.en: The adjective structural appears later, formed on structure with -al, and spread in engineering, biology and grammar in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 structural 出现较晚，由 structure 加 -al 构成，并在十九世纪扩展到工程、生物与语法领域。

items.en: Twentieth-century linguistics and anthropology made structural a key term for systems of relations, giving the word its abstract, systemic sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪的语言学与人类学使 structural 成为「关系系统」的关键术语，赋予该词抽象的、系统性的义项。

items.en: First-attestation uncertainty: the earliest English citation of structural is unknown. Reconstructed form: the Indo-European root of struere, *streu-, is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word, and its exact semantic range remains disputed.
items.cn: 首见年代存疑：structural 的英语最早书证年代不确定。重构形式：struere 的印欧语词根 *streu- 属重构，并非有记录的真实词形，其确切语义范围仍有争议。

note.en: The first group separates the structure family by part of speech and use; the second gives near-synonyms for being fundamental to a system.
note.cn: 第一组按词性与用法区分 structure 词族；第二组给出表示「属于系统根本」的近义词。

entries.definition: The arrangement itself, or the act of arranging. Structural is the adjective describing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指排列本身，或安排的动作；structural 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: Having a definite plan or pattern. Structured describes a thing that was organized; structural describes what belongs to the frame.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有明确计划或模式；structured 描述被组织好的事物，structural 描述属于框架的东西。

entries.definition: The school of thought that analyses systems of relations. Structural is the adjective; structuralism is the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 指分析关系系统的学派；structural 是形容词，structuralism 是学说。

entries.definition: The adverb answering 'in what respect?'. Structural modifies a noun; structurally modifies a verb or adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，回答「在哪方面」；structural 修饰名词，structurally 修饰动词或形容词。

entries.definition: Affecting the whole system rather than a part. It stresses spread through the system; structural stresses the framework that causes the spread.
entries.definitionCN: 指影响整个系统而非局部；systemic 强调贯穿系统，structural 强调造成这种贯穿的框架。

entries.definition: Relating to the art and design of buildings. Structural concerns whether they stand; architectural concerns how they are conceived.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑艺术与设计；structural 关心建筑能否站住，architectural 关心如何构思。

entries.definition: Relating to the way a group is arranged. It is the social counterpart of structural, which can also describe beams and molecules.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体的安排方式，是 structural 在社会领域的对应词，而 structural 也能描述梁柱与分子。

entries.definition: Serving as the base or basis. It points to what everything rests on, while structural points to how the parts are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为基础或依据，强调一切所依托之物；structural 强调部分如何连接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: structure + -al: of the frame that holds the parts together.
normal.cn: structure + -al：属于把各部分撑在一起的框架。

normal.en: The family runs structure, structured, structuralism, structuralist, restructure, infrastructure.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 structure、structured、structuralism、structuralist、restructure、infrastructure。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: structural damage, structural reform, structural adjustment, structural engineer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示范围：结构损伤、结构性改革、结构调整、结构工程师。

normal.en: A structure carries load; a structural problem is one in the load-bearing part.
normal.cn: 结构承担荷载；结构性问题就出在承重部分。

normal.en: Structural causes outlast individual choices.
normal.cn: 结构性原因比个人选择更持久。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge cut open so the beams and the arrows of load are visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥被剖开，梁柱与荷载箭头都可见。

abstract.en: Picture a building whose walls are rules rather than bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象一座建筑，墙体是规则而不是砖块。

abstract.en: Picture a skeleton inside a body, holding up everything that looks soft.
abstract.cn: 想象身体里的一副骨架，撑起所有看似柔软的部分。

examples.en: The inspection found structural cracks in three of the columns.
examples.cn: 检查发现其中三根柱子有结构裂缝。

examples.en: High youth unemployment is a structural problem, not a seasonal one.
examples.cn: 青年高失业率是结构性问题，而不是季节性问题。

examples.en: Structural biology maps the shape of proteins to explain their function.
examples.cn: 结构生物学绘制蛋白质的形状，以解释其功能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「structure（结构）+ al」——看骨架，不看表皮 → structural 结构的

root: 拉丁 struere「建造、堆叠」→ 过去分词 structus → 拉丁 structura「建筑、拼合」→ 英语 structure + -al。更深词根为重构形式 *streu-。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from arrangement in general to load-bearing frames, language systems, underlying causes, framework-changing reform, molecular shape, social inequality and literal structural damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般排列方式，扩展到承重框架、语言系统、深层原因、改变框架的改革、分子形态、社会不平等，最后回到字面上的结构损伤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visible frame carries weight from the top down to the base.
core.cn: 核心意象：可见的框架把重量从顶部一路传到基座。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AS SUCH: how the parts are put together to make a whole.
branches.cn: 排列本身：各部分如何拼合成一个整体。

branches.en: LOAD PATH: beams and foundations carry weight, and damage there endangers the whole.
branches.cn: 荷载路径：梁与基础承担重量，此处受损会危及整体。

branches.en: SYSTEMS OF RELATIONS: sounds in a language, atoms in a molecule, arranged so that form explains function.
branches.cn: 关系系统：语言中的音、分子中的原子，其排列使形式解释功能。

branches.en: CAUSES BUILT INTO INSTITUTIONS: outcomes reproduced by rules rather than by individual choice.
branches.cn: 制度内置的原因：结果由规则而非个人选择不断再生产。

branches.en: REFORM AT THE FRAME: change the rules that generate outcomes, not just the outcomes.
branches.cn: 框架层面的改革：改变产生结果的规则，而不只是结果。

intro.en: Structural is a Latin-derived base plus an adjective ending: struere 'to build' gives structura, English structure, and then structural with -al.
intro.cn: structural 是拉丁词基加形容词词尾：struere「建造」给出 structura，英语作 structure，再加 -al 成为 structural。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere and structura also underlie construct, destruction, instruct, obstruct and infrastructure, all built on the image of piling parts into a frame.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 struere 与 structura 也支撑 construct、destruction、instruct、obstruct、infrastructure，都建立在「把部件堆成框架」的意象上。

items.example: The building has structural problems in the east wing.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑东翼存在结构问题。

items.example: The structure of the argument is easy to follow.
items.exampleCN: 这一论证的结构很容易跟随。

items.example: The two buildings are structurally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两座建筑在结构上相似。

items.example: Structuralism treated language as a system of differences.
items.exampleCN: 结构主义把语言视为差异系统。

items.meaningCN: 结构主义者；结构主义的
items.example: The structuralist read the myth as a pattern of oppositions.
items.exampleCN: 这位结构主义者把神话读成对立模式。

items.meaning: to organize again in a new way
items.example: The firm restructured its debt last year.
items.exampleCN: 该公司去年重组了债务。

items.meaning: the underlying systems a society needs
items.meaningCN: 社会所依赖的基础系统
items.example: Roads and water pipes are infrastructure.
items.exampleCN: 道路与水管属于基础设施。

items.meaning: the supporting part beneath a building
items.meaningCN: 建筑物下方的支撑部分
items.example: The substructure was reinforced with steel piles.
items.exampleCN: 下部结构用钢桩加固。

definition_zh: 过时的；不再使用的；被淘汰的；废弃的；（词、法规）已不通用的
definition_en: no longer used or accepted because something newer has replaced it
core_image: 仓库角落一箱旧式接口零件还在，新到的设备上已经找不到能插进去的孔
scene: 仓库角落里还堆着一箱旧式接口零件，新到的设备上已经找不到能插进去的孔。 The warehouse still holds obsolete connectors that no current device accepts.
sceneCN: 这里指已被淘汰、不再使用（第 1 个义项：不再使用的）；句意为仓库里仍存着没有一台现役设备能接上的过时接口件。图中可辨识物件：仓库角落、旧接口零件箱、新设备、无法插入的端口。

pos.zh: 过时的；不再使用的；废弃的；被淘汰的
（少用）使废弃；使过时

derivatives.zh: 由该词干加表示过程的名词尾构成，义为「废弃；淘汰过程」
由该词干加表示「正在……的」词尾构成，义为「正逐渐淘汰的」
由该词干加动词尾构成，义为「逐渐废弃；变得过时」
由「计划的」与该名词构成，义为「有计划地使产品过时」

senses.title: No longer used
senses.definition: no longer used because something newer has taken its place
senses.definitionCN: 由于有更新之物取代而不再使用
senses.example: Gas lamps became obsolete when electric light reached the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 电灯进入街道后，煤气灯就不再使用了。
senses.why: The Latin participle means grown out of use, and this sense is its plainest survival.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「变得不被使用」，这一义项是最直白的延续。

senses.title: A word fallen out of use
senses.definition: a word that people no longer say except when reading old texts
senses.definitionCN: 人们除读旧文外已不再说的词
senses.example: The dictionary marks the word as obsolete after 1700.
senses.exampleCN: 词典把这个词标为 1700 年后已废弃。
senses.why: Language change produces the same effect as machinery: the old form still exists, but nobody reaches for it.
senses.whyCN: 语言变化造成的效果和机器一样：旧形式还在，只是没人再去取用。

senses.title: A rule no longer in force
senses.definition: a regulation that has been replaced or withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 已被替换或撤销的规章
senses.example: The clause is obsolete and should be struck from the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款已失效，应从合同中删去。
senses.why: Law keeps obsolete clauses on paper long after practice has left them.
senses.whyCN: 实践早已离开的条款，法律仍让它们留在纸上。

senses.title: A superseded machine
senses.definition: equipment that newer models have made impractical to keep
senses.definitionCN: 新机型使其继续保留已不实用的设备
senses.example: Spare parts for the obsolete printer now cost more than a new one.
senses.exampleCN: 那台淘汰打印机的配件，现在比买新的还贵。
senses.why: A machine is obsolete when fixing it costs more than replacing it.
senses.whyCN: 当修理比替换更贵，机器就被淘汰了。

senses.title: An idea left behind
senses.definition: a belief that no longer fits current knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 不再符合当今知识的看法
senses.example: The idea that memory is a single store is obsolete.
senses.exampleCN: 认为记忆是单一仓库的看法已经过时。
senses.why: Ideas age without breaking, which is why the word fits them so well.
senses.whyCN: 观念不会坏，只会老，所以这个词用在他们身上特别贴切。

senses.title: Old stock still on the shelf
senses.definition: goods kept in storage although nobody now buys them
senses.definitionCN: 虽仍存放、如今却无人购买的货物
senses.example: The shop wrote off its obsolete stock at the end of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 商店在年末把积压的淘汰存货核销。
senses.why: Stock becomes obsolete while it is still perfectly new in the box.
senses.whyCN: 存货在盒子里还崭新时，就已经成了淘汰货。

senses.title: A retired unit or currency
senses.definition: a unit of money or measure that has been withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 已被停用的货币或计量单位
senses.example: Prices were still quoted in an obsolete currency after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革之后，标价仍用已经停用的货币。
senses.why: Money and measures can be withdrawn by decree, and then the word is official.
senses.whyCN: 货币与单位可由法令停用，这时这个词是官方用语。

senses.title: A practice abandoned
senses.definition: a way of doing things that has been given up
senses.definitionCN: 已经被放弃的做事方式
senses.example: Hand-copying records by ink became obsolete once the database went live.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库上线后，用墨水手抄记录的做法就被废弃了。
senses.why: A habit disappears when the tool that carried it disappears first.
senses.whyCN: 当承载习惯的工具先消失，习惯也随之消失。

intro.en: Obsolete comes from Latin obsoletus, grown old or worn out, the past participle of obsolescere, to fall into disuse. The verb is usually explained as ob-, away, plus solere, to be accustomed, though the exact force of the prefix is described differently by different sources. English took the adjective in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 obsoletus「变旧、用坏」，是动词 obsolescere「渐不用」的过去分词。该动词通常解释为「离开」加「习惯于」，但前缀的具体作用各家说法不一。英语在十六世纪吸收了该形容词。

items.en: Solere meant to be accustomed or to be in the habit, and it stands behind the idea of usual practice.
items.cn: 这个词意为「习惯于、常有此习」，是「惯常做法」这一观念背后的词。

items.en: The verb meant to wear out or fall out of use, and its prefix suggests moving away from what was usual.
items.cn: 该动词意为用坏或渐不用，其前缀暗示从惯常状态离开。

items.en: The participle described what had already grown old and was no longer wanted.
items.cn: 该分词形容已经变旧、不再被需要之物。

items.en: French used the adjective for words and customs that had dropped away.
items.cn: 法语用它指已经消失的词与习俗。

items.en: English extended it from words to machines, laws and ideas.
items.cn: 英语把它从词语扩展到机器、法规与观念。

items.en: Manufacturing gave it the compound planned obsolescence; the phrase's first year is uncertain.
items.cn: 制造业给出复合说法「有计划地淘汰」；该说法首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the grown-out-of-use root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of being out of date. The note warns that absolute is a look-alike from an unrelated root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「用旧而废」词根或形近；第二组指其他「过时」的说法。这里提醒：形近的「绝对」一词出自不相干的词根。

entries.definition: The process of becoming outdated.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐过时的过程。

entries.definition: In the process of becoming obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在走向淘汰的。

entries.definition: To grow obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 指变得过时。

entries.definition: Complete and unconditional; it comes from a verb meaning to loosen or set free, not from being accustomed.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全且无条件的；出自表示「解开、释放」的动词，与「习惯于」无关。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned but possibly still usable.
entries.definitionCN: 指样式老但可能仍可使用。

entries.definition: Very old and no longer suitable, often said of systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指非常老旧且已不适用，常用于制度。

entries.definition: No longer in fashion or no longer the accepted way.
entries.definitionCN: 指不再流行或不再是被接受的方式。

entries.definition: No longer existing or operating, said of organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 指已不存在或停止运作，用于机构。

entries.definition: Replaced by something that does the job better.
entries.definitionCN: 指被做得更好的东西取代。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier period and retained only in special contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于较早时期、只在特殊语境中保留。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the box of connectors, the gas lamp, the struck-out contract clause and the written-off stock.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用那箱接口件、煤气灯、被划掉的合同条款与核销的存货。

normal.en: Obsolete does not mean broken; it means nobody reaches for it any more.
normal.cn: 「过时」不等于坏了，而是没人再去取用它。

normal.en: A gas lamp still lights, but the street is wired for electricity.
normal.cn: 煤气灯仍能亮，可街上已经通了电。

normal.en: The word and the machine share one fate: both are outgrown.
normal.cn: 词语与机器命运相同：都被长过了头。

normal.en: Planned obsolescence is obsolescence with a schedule and a budget.
normal.cn: 「有计划地淘汰」，就是带着日程与预算的淘汰。

normal.en: Absolute looks close but belongs to loosening, not to growing old.
normal.cn: 形近的那个词属于「解开」，不属于「变旧」。

abstract.en: Usefulness is a relationship between a thing and a moment, and moments move.
abstract.cn: 有用是物与时刻之间的关系，而时刻会走。

abstract.en: Every generation inherits tools it must first learn to stop using.
abstract.cn: 每一代人都继承了一批必须先学会不再使用的工具。

abstract.en: What becomes obsolete usually leaves a word behind that outlives it.
abstract.cn: 被淘汰的东西，往往留下一个比它活得更久的词。

examples.en: The format is obsolete, and the archive can no longer open the files.
examples.cn: 这种格式已经过时，档案馆再也打不开那些文件。

examples.en: New scanning software rendered the old index cards obsolete overnight.
examples.cn: 新的扫描软件一夜之间让旧索引卡被淘汰。

examples.en: Using that term today sounds obsolete even in legal writing.
examples.cn: 今天再用那个词，即便在法律文书里也显得过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥伯索利特」：旧东西还在架上，只是没人再伸手去拿，慢慢就「废」了

root: 源于拉丁语表示「习惯于」的动词，其复合动词义为「渐不用、用坏」，过去分词义为「变旧废弃的」，经法语进入英语。该前缀的具体作用各家解释不一。十六世纪进入英语；「有计划地淘汰」一语首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow disuse: an unused thing, a dead word, a withdrawn rule, a superseded machine, a left-behind idea, unsold stock, a retired unit, and an abandoned practice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「不再使用」展开：闲置之物、废弃的词、撤销的规定、被取代的机器、被抛下的观念、卖不掉的存货、停用的单位与放弃的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the box of connectors that no new machine has a port for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一箱接口件，新机器上找不到能插的孔。

branches.en: THE RETIRED THING: an object or machine that newer things replaced.
branches.cn: 退役之物：被更新之物取代的器物或机器。

branches.en: THE RETIRED WORD AND IDEA: what people no longer say or believe.
branches.cn: 退役的词与观念：人们不再说、也不再信的东西。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE LEFT ON PAPER: a rule that practice has already abandoned.
branches.cn: 留在纸上的条款：实践早已放弃的规则。

branches.en: THE SHELF AND THE HABIT: stock nobody buys, practices nobody follows.
branches.cn: 货架与习惯：无人购买的存货、无人沿用的做法。

branches.en: THE WITHDRAWN UNIT: money or measures taken out of use by decree.
branches.cn: 撤销的单位：由法令停用的货币或计量单位。

intro.en: Obsolete is a Latin participle used as an English adjective; its family covers the process of going out of use and the schedule that produces it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁分词用作英语形容词；词族覆盖「走向废弃」的过程，以及制造这一过程的日程。

latinIntro.en: Latin solere and obsolescere supply the habit and the falling away from it; the participle obsoletus gives the English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「习惯于」与「渐不用」提供「习惯」与「离开习惯」两层意思；分词给出英语形态。

items.example: It supplies the idea of usual practice.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「惯常做法」的意思。

items.example: It marks movement away from the usual.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「离开常态」的方向。

items.example: The verb of decay behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是词背后的「衰废」动词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective directly.
items.exampleCN: 它直接给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It forms obsolescence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「淘汰过程」。

items.example: It forms obsolescent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「正走向淘汰的」。

items.example: It forms the rare verb obsolesce.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少用的动词「变得过时」。

items.example: A commercial phrase built on the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 由该形容词构成的商业说法。

derivatives.zh: 由该词干加表示过程的名词尾构成，义为「淘汰过程」
由该词干加表示「正在……」的词尾构成，义为「正走向淘汰的」
由该词干加动词尾构成，义为「变得过时」
由「计划的」与该名词构成，义为「有计划地使产品过时」

definition_zh: 连续的；接连的；连贯的；结果性的
definition_en: following one after another without an interruption, or following as a result
core_image: 日历上六页接连翻过，每一页的日期都紧挨着前一页，中间没有空白的一页
scene: 跑道上电子计时牌一站一站翻过，同一名选手的名字连续出现，中间没有空缺。 She won the title for three consecutive seasons.
sceneCN: 这里指一段时间内一次接一次、中间没有断开（第 1 个义项：时间上接连无间断）；句意为她连续三个赛季夺得冠军。图中可辨识物件：电子计时牌、选手名次、连成一列的赛季记录。

pos.zh: 连续的；接连的；连贯的；结果性的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「连续地；接连地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「连续性」
由同一拉丁词干构成的名词，义为「连续；顺序」
由表示否定的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不连续的」

senses.title: Following in time without a break
senses.definition: happening in one period after another with nothing missing in between
senses.definitionCN: 一个时段接一个时段地发生，中间没有缺失
senses.example: The team trained for five consecutive days before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前，这支队伍连续训练了五天。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to follow closely, so the word begins with one thing pressing right behind another.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为紧跟，因此这个词最初就是一物紧贴另一物之后。

senses.title: Counting in an unbroken run
senses.definition: used of numbers or amounts that follow in an unbroken order
senses.definitionCN: 用于按不间断次序相随的数字或数量
senses.example: Write the consecutive numbers from one to ten.
senses.exampleCN: 写出一到十的连续数字。
senses.why: Counting is the plainest example of following on, with no value skipped between two terms.
senses.whyCN: 计数是「依次相随」最朴素的例子，两个数之间没有跳过的值。

senses.title: A run of wins
senses.definition: describing victories or successes that come one after another without a defeat between them
senses.definitionCN: 指一场接一场的胜利或成功，中间没有失败
senses.example: The club recorded four consecutive victories in the league.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部在联赛中取得四连胜。
senses.why: Sport counts streaks, and a streak is exactly a series with no gap in it.
senses.whyCN: 体育要数连续纪录，而连续纪录正是一个没有缺口的序列。

senses.title: Adjacent in a series
senses.definition: placed next to each other in an ordered set, as with numbers or seats
senses.definitionCN: 在有序集合中彼此相邻，如号码或座位
senses.example: The tickets bear consecutive serial numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些票的编号是连号的。
senses.why: When items are numbered, following on means occupying the very next place.
senses.whyCN: 当物件被编号时，依次相随便意味着占据紧接着的那一位。

senses.title: A chain of linked events
senses.definition: describing events in which each one follows from the one before it
senses.definitionCN: 指每个事件都由前一个事件引出的情形
senses.example: The report describes a consecutive chain of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一连串前后相承的失误。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant to result from, so following in time can become following as a consequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词也意为「由……导致」，因此时间上的相随可以变成因果上的相承。

senses.title: The grammar of result
senses.definition: naming a clause that expresses the result of what the main clause states
senses.definitionCN: 指表达主句所述内容之结果的从句
senses.example: The grammar book explains how a consecutive clause expresses result.
senses.exampleCN: 这本语法书讲解结果从句如何表达结果。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the adjective for clauses where the second statement follows from the first.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借这个形容词指第二个陈述由第一个陈述引出的从句。

senses.title: Unbroken shifts or operation
senses.definition: describing work periods that run one after another without a pause
senses.definitionCN: 指一个接一个运行、中间不停顿的工作时段
senses.example: The plant runs three consecutive shifts during the peak season.
senses.exampleCN: 生产旺季，工厂连续开三个班次。
senses.why: Industry measures time in shifts, and consecutive shifts leave no idle gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 工业以班次计量时间，而连续班次之间没有空闲的间隔。

senses.title: Year-after-year climate records
senses.definition: used of weather or climate data gathered over an unbroken series of years
senses.definitionCN: 用于在连续多年中收集的天气或气候数据
senses.example: Records show three consecutive dry years in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 记录显示该地区连续三年干旱。
senses.why: Climate science compares year to year, and a run of years with no break is the basic unit of a trend.
senses.whyCN: 气候科学逐年比较，而一段没有中断的年份正是趋势的基本单位。

intro.en: Consecutive comes from Latin consequi, to follow closely, from con-, together, and sequi, to follow; the past participle consecutus produced Late Latin consecutivus, which English borrowed in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「consequi」紧跟、随后，由「con-」一起与「sequi」跟随构成；过去分词「consecutus」产生晚期拉丁语「consecutivus」，英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: To follow is the core of the word, and the same verb stands behind sequence and sequel.
items.cn: 跟随是这个词的核心，同一个动词也构成「sequence」与「sequel」的词源。

items.en: The prefix means together or along with, so following becomes following on.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为一起或随之，于是「跟随」变成「紧跟着」。

items.en: The verb meant to follow closely, to come after, and also to result from something.
items.cn: 这个动词意为紧跟、随后，也意为由某事物导致。

items.en: The past participle described what has followed, and it is the stem before the English ending.
items.cn: 这个过去分词描述已经跟随而来的事物，是英语词尾之前的词干。

items.en: The later adjective named things that follow in order or form a series.
items.cn: 这个晚期形容词指按次序相随或构成序列的事物。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century for things coming one after another.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个形容词，用于一个接一个到来的事物。

note.en: The first group looks like consecutive or shares its Latin stem; the second group names neighbouring ideas of things following in order. Note that successive stresses the order of items, from Latin sub- and cedere, to come after, while consecutive stresses that no gap separates them.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「consecutive」相近或共享拉丁词干；第二组是与「依次跟随」相邻的说法。要注意「successive」强调各项的次序，出自拉丁语「sub-」与「cedere」跟随在后；而「consecutive」强调中间没有间隔。

entries.definition: In an unbroken order, one after another.
entries.definitionCN: 指不间断地依次发生。

entries.definition: The state of following in sequence, a rare noun from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指依次相随的状态，是同一词干的罕见名词。

entries.definition: The quality of being unbroken in sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指序列不中断的性质。

entries.definition: A result that follows from an action; it shares the Latin verb but not the sense of sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指由行为引出的结果；共享拉丁动词，但没有「连续」之义。

entries.definition: To set something apart as sacred; it looks close but belongs to a word for making sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物定为神圣；形近但属于「使神圣」那一系。

entries.definition: Following in order, one after another, with emphasis on the sequence rather than on gaps.
entries.definitionCN: 指依次相随，强调次序，而不强调有无间隔。

entries.definition: Arranged in a fixed order, one step or item after another.
entries.definitionCN: 指按固定次序排列，一步或一项接一项。

entries.definition: Going on without any stop or break, often of time or movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指不停顿、不中断，常用于时间或运动。

entries.definition: Not broken off at any point, used of a stretch of time or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指一段时间或活动在任何节点都未被打断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin follow verb behind the word, its real family and the everyday things counted in runs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的拉丁语「跟随」动词、真实同族词，以及日常中成串计数的事物。

normal.en: The Latin sequi is to follow, and con- adds the sense of coming right along after.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「sequi」是跟随，「con-」加上「紧随其后」的意思。

normal.en: Consecutive days, consecutive years and consecutive wins all count things with no gap.
normal.cn: 连续几天、连续数年与连胜，数的都是没有缺口的事物。

normal.en: Consecutive numbers are neighbours on the number line, like adjacent seats in a row.
normal.cn: 连号数字是数轴上的邻居，就像一排里相邻的座位。

normal.en: A consecutive clause is named for the result that follows from the main statement.
normal.cn: 结果从句得名于由主句陈述引出的结果。

normal.en: Consecutive interpreting follows speech in chunks, one stretch after another.
normal.cn: 交替传译跟着讲话分段进行，一段接一段。

abstract.en: A gap is the only enemy of this word: if one day is missing, the run is broken.
abstract.cn: 缺口是这个词唯一的敌人：只要缺了一天，连续就断了。

abstract.en: Time is not a line but a stack of pages, and consecutive means no page was torn out.
abstract.cn: 时间不是一条线，而是一叠纸页，连续就意味着没有一页被撕掉。

abstract.en: A streak is fragile because it is counted backwards; one loss erases the whole series.
abstract.cn: 连续纪录之所以脆弱，是因为它被倒着数；一场失利就抹掉整串。

examples.en: The region suffered three consecutive summers of drought.
examples.cn: 该地区连续三个夏天遭遇干旱。

examples.en: Her consecutive victories surprised the whole circuit.
examples.cn: 她的连胜让整个巡回赛都感到意外。

examples.en: Number the pages in consecutive order from front to back.
examples.cn: 把书页从前往后按连续顺序编号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「肯塞丘提夫」——一个接一个，中间不空档：连续的、接连的

root: 拉丁语「consequi」意为紧跟、随后，由「con-」一起加「sequi」跟随构成，过去分词「consecutus」，晚期拉丁语「consecutivus」；英语十七世纪引入。它与「secare」切无关，因此与「section」「sector」不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from time to counting to sport: unbroken time, counting, a run of wins, adjacent items, a chain of causes, the result clause, unbroken shifts, and year-by-year climate records.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从时间走到计数再走到体育：不间断的时间、连续计数、连胜、相邻项、因果链、结果从句、连续班次，以及逐年气候记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: calendar pages turn in a stack, each date touching the next with no blank page between.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历一叠页接连翻过，每个日期都紧贴下一个，中间没有空白页。

branches.en: THE UNBROKEN STRETCH: time or a count runs on with nothing missing.
branches.cn: 不间断的一段：时间或计数一路延续，什么都不缺。

branches.en: THE RUN AND THE SERIES: wins stack up, and neighbouring items share an edge.
branches.cn: 连续纪录与序列：胜利层层累积，相邻各项共用一条边。

branches.en: THE CHAIN OF CAUSES: one event follows another as its outcome.
branches.cn: 因果链：一个事件作为结果跟随另一个事件。

branches.en: THE GRAMMATICAL RESULT: a clause states what follows from the main clause.
branches.cn: 语法上的结果：从句陈述由主句引出的内容。

branches.en: THE WORKING AND CLIMATE RECORD: unbroken shifts, and statistics over year after year.
branches.cn: 作业与气候记录：连续的班次，以及逐年累积的统计。

intro.en: Consecutive is a Latin adjective of following, and its endings and prefixes keep the sense of a series with no break.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示跟随的拉丁形容词，它的词尾与前缀都保留着「序列不断」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies sequi, to follow, and consequi, to follow closely; the adjective consecutivus comes from the past participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「sequi」跟随与「consequi」紧跟；形容词「consecutivus」来自其过去分词。

items.example: The verb is the root of sequence and sequel as well.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也是「sequence」与「sequel」的词根。

items.example: The prefix makes following into following on.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」变成「紧跟着」。

items.structure: Latin verb from con- and sequi
items.example: The verb joins the two halves of the idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把这一意思的两半合在一起。

items.example: The participle supplies the stem of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了形容词的词干。

items.example: The form passed through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式经法语进入英语。

items.example: It marks the English adjective consecutive.
items.exampleCN: 它标出英语形容词「consecutive」。

items.example: It forms the adverb consecutively.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词「consecutively」。

items.example: It forms the noun consecutiveness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成名词「consecutiveness」。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from con- and sequi

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「连续地」
由同一拉丁词干构成的名词，义为「连续；顺序」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「连续性」
由表示否定的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不连续的」

definition_en: fluent and forceful in speech; showing feeling or proof clearly without many words

intro.en: Eloquent is Latin eloquens, the participle of eloqui, which joins ex- meaning out to loqui meaning to speak; it describes someone who speaks out well.
intro.cn: eloquent 就是拉丁语 eloquens，eloqui 的分词，而 eloqui 把 ex-（向外）与 loqui（说话）结合；它形容把话说得好的人。

items.en: Latin loqui means to speak.
items.cn: 拉丁语 loqui 意为说话。

items.en: Adding ex- gives eloqui, to speak out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 eloqui，意为说出来。

items.en: The participle eloquens means speaking out well.
items.cn: 分词 eloquens 意为把话说得好的。

items.en: English took eloquent in the 14C for a persuasive speaker.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 eloquent，指有说服力的演讲者。

items.en: Writers applied eloquent to looks, gestures and silence.
items.cn: 作家把 eloquent 用于眼神、手势与沉默。

items.en: Lawyers used eloquent for facts that prove a point without argument.
items.cn: 律师用 eloquent 指无需论证就能说明问题的事实。

note.en: Eloquent and loquacious share loqui, the Latin root for speak; eloquent speaks well and persuades, loquacious simply speaks a great deal.
note.cn: eloquent 与 loquacious 共用 loqui，那是拉丁语「说话」的词根；eloquent 说得好且能说服人，loquacious 只是说得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: eloquent ＝ e-（向外）＋ loqu（说话，拉丁 loqui）＋ -ent（形容词后缀）＝「能把话说出来的」。名词 eloquence，副词 eloquently。三层用法按「谁在说」分：人 an eloquent speaker 雄辩的演讲者；言辞 an eloquent speech 雄辩的演讲；无声之物 eloquent silence 意味深长的沉默、an eloquent look 传情的一瞥、eloquent proof 明白有力的证据。固定结构 eloquent of ＋ 名词＝「明白显示出…」：a face eloquent of despair 一张写满绝望的脸。比较级用 more eloquent，没有 eloquenter。近义 articulate 强调表达清楚有条理，persuasive 强调能说服，expressive 强调表情达意；loquacious 只是话多，未必说得好。

definition_zh: 测量；量出；尺寸；措施；分寸；程度；节拍；格律

senses.title: To find a size or amount
senses.definition: to find the size, length, weight or amount of something by using a tool or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 用工具或标准求出某物的尺寸、长度、重量或数量
senses.example: Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
senses.exampleCN: 木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to measure, and the physical act of comparing against a standard is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本意就是测量，拿某物与标准相比较的实体动作是最古老的一层。

senses.title: The number obtained
senses.definition: the size or amount that a measurement produces, often written as a figure with a unit
senses.definitionCN: 测量得出的尺寸或数量，常写成带单位的数字
senses.example: The measure came out at two metres, not one.
senses.exampleCN: 量出来的结果是一点九米，不是一米。
senses.why: A measurement is both the act and its outcome, so the noun carries the number as well as the procedure.
senses.whyCN: 测量既是动作也是结果，因此这个名词既携带数字，也携带过程。

senses.title: A step taken to fix something
senses.titleCN: 为解决问题所采取的步骤
senses.definition: an action or policy adopted to deal with a problem or to reach an aim
senses.definitionCN: 为处理问题或达到目的而采取的行动或政策
senses.example: The city took measures to cut traffic at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 市里采取措施减少校门口的交通。
senses.why: A step is a measured amount of action: enough to change the situation, not more, and the metaphor runs from dose to policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个步骤就是定量的行动：足以改变局面，又不过量，这个比喻从剂量一直走到政策。

senses.title: A proposed law
senses.definition: in a legislature, a proposed law put forward for debate and vote
senses.definitionCN: 在立法机构中提交辩论与表决的法律草案
senses.example: The measure passed by three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票之差通过。
senses.why: A bill is a measured response written into legal form, and American usage kept the word for the draft itself.
senses.whyCN: 法案是把有分寸的应对写成法律形式，美式用法保留了这个词来指草案本身。

senses.title: A standard for comparison
senses.definition: a standard, unit or benchmark by which other things are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断其他事物的标准、单位或基准
senses.example: Test scores are a crude measure of a school.
senses.exampleCN: 考试分数是对学校的一种粗略衡量。
senses.why: To measure anything one needs a fixed unit, and the noun then names any yardstick, including an abstract one.
senses.whyCN: 要测量任何东西都需要固定单位，名词随后指任何标尺，包括抽象的标尺。

senses.title: A degree or extent
senses.definition: the extent to which something is true or present, as in in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 某事物为真或存在的程度，如「在很大程度上」
senses.example: The success was in large measure due to the technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 这次成功在很大程度上要归功于技术人员。
senses.why: An amount can be spoken of without a ruler, so the word extends from physical quantity to degree of influence.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以不用尺子来说，于是这个词从物理量扩展到影响的程度。

senses.title: A limit or moderation
senses.definition: a proper limit in behaviour or feeling, or the absence of one in beyond measure
senses.definitionCN: 行为或情感上应有的限度，或在「无法估量」中表示没有限度
senses.example: His anger went beyond measure.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒到了无法估量的地步。
senses.why: The idea of a fixed amount turns moral: to keep measure is to keep within bounds, and to exceed it is to lose proportion.
senses.whyCN: 固定数量的观念转向道德：守分寸就是守在界限内，越过就是失去比例。

senses.title: A bar in music
senses.definition: a group of beats between two bar lines, the unit of musical time
senses.definitionCN: 两条小节线之间的一组拍子，是音乐时间的基本单位
senses.example: The phrase fits one measure of four beats.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐句正好占一小节四拍。
senses.why: Music divides time into equal measured spans, so the word for measuring became the name of the span.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把时间分成等长的段，于是表示测量的词成了那一段的名字。

senses.title: The metre of a line
senses.definition: the patterned rhythm of a line of verse, counted in feet
senses.definitionCN: 诗句中有规律的节奏，以音步计数
senses.example: The poem keeps a steady measure through twelve lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗十二行都保持稳定的格律。
senses.why: Verse counts syllables the way a ruler counts inches, and the noun for the count became the name of the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 诗句像尺子量英寸那样数音节，表示计数的名词就成了这种模式的名字。

intro.en: Measure comes from Old French mesure, from Latin mensura 'a measuring', built on metiri 'to measure'. The root is generally connected with a very old word for measure that also gave Greek metron and English metre.
intro.cn: measure 来自古法语 mesure，源头是拉丁语 mensura「测量」，由 metiri「测量」构成。这个词根一般认为与一个极古老的「度量」词相关，希腊语 metron 与英语 metre 也出自它。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure or apportion, and it is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: metiri 意为测量、按量分配，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Mensura named the act and the result of measuring, and it passed through French as the English noun.
items.cn: mensura 指测量的动作与结果，经法语成为英语名词。

items.en: The old root is generally reconstructed as a word for measure, the same one behind metre and metric; the reconstruction is accepted but the exact shape is source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个古老词根一般被重构为表示「度量」的词，metre 与 metric 也出自它；这一重构被接受，但确切形态来源不确定。

items.en: Old French mesure carried both the physical and the moral senses, and English took the pair together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mesure 同时带有物理与道德两层意思，英语在十三世纪把两者一起接收。

items.en: American usage of the eighteenth century applied measure to a proposed law, a use that British English largely dropped.
items.cn: 十八世纪的美式用法把这个词用到法律草案上，英式英语后来大体放弃了这一用法。

items.en: Latin mensura had already named the counted span in rhythm, and English kept measure for a bar and for metrical pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mensura 早已用来指节奏中被数出的段落，英语保留 measure 指小节与格律。

note.en: The first group shares the measuring root; the second group names related actions or quantities.
note.cn: 第一组共享「测量」词根；第二组是相关动作或数量。

entries.definition: The act or the figure produced by measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 测量的动作，或测量得出的数字。

entries.definition: Large or stable enough to be measured.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或稳定到可以被测量的。

entries.definition: Deliberate and restrained, as if each step were weighed.
entries.definitionCN: 审慎而有节制的，仿佛每一步都称过。

entries.definition: The process, or a compound for a tool such as a measuring tape.
entries.definitionCN: 测量过程，或构成卷尺一类工具名。

entries.definition: The mathematics of lengths, areas and volumes; a learned doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的数学；学术性的同源词。

entries.definition: To estimate or measure, often with an instrument; also the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 估计或测量，常借助仪器；也指该仪器。

entries.definition: To express something as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物表示为数字。

entries.definition: To judge the value or level of something, with less emphasis on units.
entries.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或水平，对单位的强调较少。

entries.definition: An action taken toward a goal, the everyday word behind the policy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目标而采取的行动，是政策义背后的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin measuring verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of policy and tools.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语测量动词、真实同族词，以及政策与工具里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin metiri meant to measure, and mensura gave English the noun through French.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，mensura 经法语给了英语这个名词。

normal.en: The family runs measure, measurement, measurable, measured and measuring.
normal.cn: 同族词有 measure、measurement、measurable、measured 与 measuring。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: take measures, safety measures, in large measure, beyond measure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：采取措施、安全措施、在很大程度上、无法估量地。

normal.en: A tape measure is the tool, and a measure of success is the standard: one word, two kinds of ruler.
normal.cn: 卷尺是工具，衡量成功的标准是标尺：同一个词，两种尺。

normal.en: Music counts beats into a measure, and verse counts feet into a measure.
normal.cn: 音乐把拍子数成小节，诗句把音步数成格律。

abstract.en: To keep measure is to know how much is enough, which is a moral skill before it is a mathematical one.
abstract.cn: 守分寸就是知道多少算够，这先是道德的技能，然后才是数学的。

abstract.en: What can be measured is not always what matters, and what matters is not always measurable.
abstract.cn: 可测量的不总是重要的，重要的也不总是可测量的。

abstract.en: A measure is a decision about what counts, made before any number appears.
abstract.cn: 尺度是在数字出现之前，关于「什么算数」的决定。

examples.en: The nurse measured the wound and wrote the figure in the chart.
examples.cn: 护士量了伤口的大小，把数字写进病历。

examples.en: The council adopted three measures to reduce waste.
examples.cn: 议会通过三项措施减少浪费。

examples.en: Her patience was tested beyond measure that afternoon.
examples.cn: 那天下午，她的耐心受到了无法估量的考验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「米热」——用尺子一点点比过去，看看到底有多长：测量

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「测量、量度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure。词根一般认为与古希腊语 metron 同源，确切形态属重构，来源不确定；法案、小节与格律义均为后起扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one ruler: the act of measuring, the number it gives, a policy step, a bill, a standard, a degree of influence, a moral limit, a musical bar and a line's metre.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一把尺：测量的动作、量出的数字、政策步骤、法案、比较标准、影响程度、道德限度、音乐小节与诗句格律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape is laid along the desk, and the number goes straight onto the cutting list.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺贴住桌沿，数字直接写进下料单。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE FIGURE: laying a tape down, and the number that comes back.
branches.cn: 动作与数字：把尺子贴上去，以及报回来的那个数。

branches.en: THE POLICY DOSE: a step sized to the problem, and the same step written as a bill.
branches.cn: 政策剂量：按问题大小配出的步骤，以及写成法案的同一步骤。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: test scores used as a crude ruler for a school.
branches.cn: 标尺：把考试分数当作衡量学校的粗尺。

senses.title: High-energy particles from space
senses.definition: the general name for energetic particles and rays arriving at the earth from outside its atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 对从大气层之外到达地球的高能粒子与射线的总称
senses.example: Cosmic radiation arrives at the top of the atmosphere from every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙辐射从各个方向到达大气层顶部。
senses.why: A single umbrella term was needed once balloon flights showed that ionisation increased with altitude.
senses.whyCN: 当气球观测显示电离随高度增加后，就需要一个统称。

senses.title: Primary cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the original particles arriving from space before they interact with the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 在与大气发生作用之前从太空到达的原始粒子
senses.example: Primary cosmic radiation consists mostly of protons stripped of their electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 初级宇宙辐射主要由失去电子的质子组成。
senses.why: Dividing primary from secondary separates what space sends from what the air makes.
senses.whyCN: 把初级与次级分开，就把太空送来的东西与空气生成的东西区别开来。

senses.title: Secondary cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the cascade of particles produced when primary radiation strikes air molecules
senses.definitionCN: 初级辐射撞击空气分子时产生的粒子级联
senses.example: Secondary cosmic radiation forms a shower of particles when the primary hits air.
senses.exampleCN: 当初级粒子撞上空气时，次级宇宙辐射形成粒子簇射。
senses.why: By the time radiation reaches sea level almost none of it is primary, so the distinction matters for measurement.
senses.whyCN: 当辐射到达海平面时几乎已没有初级粒子，因此这一区分对测量很重要。

senses.title: Galactic cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the component accelerated elsewhere in the galaxy, arriving steadily from outside the solar system
senses.definitionCN: 在银河系其他地方被加速、从太阳系之外稳定到达的成分
senses.example: Galactic cosmic radiation comes from outside the solar system and varies slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 银河宇宙辐射来自太阳系之外，变化缓慢。
senses.why: Its steadiness makes it a baseline against which solar outbursts stand out.
senses.whyCN: 它的稳定使它成为基准，太阳爆发在对比下便显得突出。

senses.title: Solar cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the particles accelerated by the sun, especially during flares and coronal mass ejections
senses.definitionCN: 由太阳加速的粒子，尤其在耀斑与日冕物质抛射期间
senses.example: Solar cosmic radiation surges during a large flare.
senses.exampleCN: 在一次大耀斑期间，太阳宇宙辐射会骤增。
senses.why: The sun is a local and variable source, so its contribution is named separately.
senses.whyCN: 太阳是局部的、变化的源，因此它的贡献被单独命名。

senses.title: Dose in aviation and spaceflight
senses.titleCN: 航空与航天的辐射剂量
senses.definition: the accumulated exposure received by aircrews and astronauts from cosmic radiation
senses.definitionCN: 机组人员与航天员从宇宙辐射中累积受到的照射
senses.example: Aircrews receive more cosmic radiation than people on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 机组人员受到的宇宙辐射比地面人员更多。
senses.why: Shielding by air is thinner at altitude, so the same sky delivers a larger dose.
senses.whyCN: 高空的空气屏蔽更薄，同一片天空因此送来更大的剂量。

senses.title: Effects on electronics
senses.definition: single-particle upsets in circuits caused by an energetic particle strike
senses.definitionCN: 高能粒子撞击引起的电路单粒子翻转
senses.example: A single particle of cosmic radiation can flip a bit in a memory chip.
senses.exampleCN: 一个宇宙辐射粒子就能翻转存储芯片中的一位。
senses.why: Miniaturised circuits hold so little charge that one strike now matters.
senses.whyCN: 微型化电路所存电荷极少，一次撞击便足以造成影响。

senses.title: Cosmogenic nuclides and dating
senses.definition: rare isotopes produced in rock by cosmic radiation, used to date exposure surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 岩石中由宇宙辐射产生的稀有同位素，用于给暴露面测年
senses.example: Cosmogenic nuclides produced by cosmic radiation allow surfaces to be dated.
senses.exampleCN: 由宇宙辐射产生的宇宙成因核素使地表得以测年。
senses.why: The sky leaves a slow chemical clock in stone, and the clock can be read.
senses.whyCN: 天空在石头里留下一只缓慢的化学钟，而这钟可以被读出。

senses.title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the rarest particles, carrying energies far beyond anything built on earth can produce
senses.definitionCN: 最稀少的粒子，其能量远超地球上任何人造装置所能产生
senses.example: Ultra-high-energy cosmic radiation is rare but carries more energy than any accelerator can reach.
senses.exampleCN: 超高能宇宙辐射很稀少，却携带比任何加速器都高的能量。
senses.why: At the far end of the energy range, the rarity itself becomes the scientific problem.
senses.whyCN: 在能量范围的最远端，稀少本身成了科学问题。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek adjective for the ordered universe to a Latin noun for the act of sending out rays. Both halves are well attested; the phrase itself dates from the era when balloon flights first detected the radiation, so its first use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示有序宇宙的希腊形容词，与一个表示发出射线的拉丁名词组合起来。两半来源均有据；短语本身产生于气球升空首次探测到该辐射的年代，确切首见为约数。

items.en: Kosmos meant order, ornament and, by extension, the world as an ordered whole.
items.cn: 这个词表示秩序、装饰，引申指作为有序整体的世界。

items.en: The adjective described anything belonging to that ordered whole.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述属于那个有序整体的事物。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke of a wheel and then a ray of light.
items.cn: 这个词先指车轮的辐条，后指光线。

items.en: The verb meant to emit rays or to shine.
items.cn: 这个动词意为发出射线或发光。

items.en: English formed the noun for the emission and for the energy emitted.
items.cn: 英语由此构成名词，指发射行为与被发射的能量。

items.en: Before the First World War, balloon flights showed that ionisation rose with altitude, and the phrase for the source soon followed.
items.cn: 在第一次世界大战之前，气球飞行显示电离随高度上升，指称这一来源的短语随即出现。

note.cn: 第一组共享形容词「宇宙的」，或容易与之混淆；第二组指相同或相关的高能粒子。

entries.definition: Tiny solid grains drifting between the stars.
entries.definitionCN: 在星际间飘浮的微小固体颗粒。

entries.definition: Funny, or relating to comedy.

entries.definition: Relating to beauty treatment or superficial change.
entries.definitionCN: 与美容或表面修饰相关的。

entries.definition: The universe as an ordered whole.
entries.definitionCN: 作为有序整体的宇宙。

entries.definition: Radiation energetic enough to strip electrons from atoms.
entries.definitionCN: 能量足以从原子中剥离电子的辐射。

entries.definition: The radiation environment beyond the atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 大气层之外的辐射环境。

entries.definition: Radiation originating within the galaxy.
entries.definitionCN: 源自银河系内部的辐射。

entries.definition: Particles travelling at close to the speed of light.
entries.definitionCN: 以接近光速运动的粒子。

entries.definition: The ordinary low-level radiation present in an environment.
entries.definitionCN: 环境中普遍存在的低强度辐射。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the particle from space to the ground; abstract ones treat the word as an invisible rain that never stops.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着粒子从太空到地面的路径展开；抽象联想把这个词看作一场永不停歇的看不见的雨。

normal.en: A balloon rises and the ionisation meter climbs: that is cosmic radiation.
normal.cn: 气球升高，电离计读数上升，那就是宇宙辐射。

normal.en: Primary particles come from space; secondary ones are made in the air.
normal.cn: 初级粒子来自太空，次级粒子在空气中生成。

normal.en: The galaxy sends a steady background; the sun sends sudden surges.
normal.cn: 银河送来稳定的背景，太阳送来突发的骤增。

normal.en: At cruising altitude the thin air shields less, so the dose rises.
normal.cn: 在巡航高度空气稀薄、屏蔽更弱，因此剂量上升。

normal.en: One stray particle can flip a bit in a memory chip.
normal.cn: 一个游离的粒子就能翻转存储芯片中的一位。

abstract.en: Cosmic radiation is a rain with no clouds and no shelter.
abstract.cn: 宇宙辐射是一场没有云也没有屋檐的雨。

abstract.en: Anything that arrives from everywhere at once becomes a background rather than an event.
abstract.cn: 凡从各处同时到达者，便成了背景而非事件。

abstract.en: The rarest particles carry the largest questions.
abstract.cn: 最稀少的粒子承载着最大的问题。

examples.en: High-altitude flights increase the crew's exposure to cosmic radiation.
examples.cn: 高空飞行增加了机组人员受到的宇宙辐射。

examples.en: The detector recorded cosmic radiation throughout the night.
examples.cn: 探测器整夜记录着宇宙辐射。

examples.en: Thick rock shields underground labs from cosmic radiation.
examples.cn: 厚实的岩层为地下实验室屏蔽了宇宙辐射。

dict_mnemonic.text: cosmic（宇宙的）+ radiation（辐射）——来自宇宙的辐射，即宇宙辐射

root: 由 cosmic 与 radiation 组合。前者源自希腊语 kosmos「秩序、世界」；后者源自拉丁语 radius「辐条、光线」及其动词 radiare「发光、发射线」。短语随二十世纪初气球观测发现高空电离增强而出现，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one shower of particles from its origin to its effects: the whole flux, its primary and secondary parts, its galactic and solar sources, its doses, its damage, its clock and its rarest end.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟踪同一场粒子雨，从来源追到影响：整体通量、初级与次级、银河与太阳来源、剂量、损伤、测年之钟与最稀少的一端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a detector on a plateau, counting invisible arrivals.
core.cn: 核心意象：高原上的探测器，在数着看不见的来客。

branches.en: THE CORE SPLIT: one arriving flux, divided into what space sent and what the air made.
branches.cn: 核心划分：同一股到达的通量，分为太空送来的与空气生成的。

branches.en: THE TWO SOURCES: a steady galactic background and sudden solar surges.
branches.cn: 两个来源：稳定的银河背景与突发的太阳骤增。

branches.en: THE HUMAN DOSE: aircrews and astronauts receive more of it.
branches.cn: 人体剂量：机组与航天员受到更多照射。

branches.en: THE TWO TRACES: flipped bits in circuits and rare isotopes in stone.
branches.cn: 两种痕迹：电路中翻转的位与石头中的稀有同位素。

branches.en: THE EXTREME: particles too energetic for any earthly machine.
branches.cn: 极端一端：能量高到任何地球装置都无法产生的粒子。

items.exampleCN: 它把宇宙命名为被安排而非随机的东西。

items.example: The verb supplies the English verb and noun of radiation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了英语的动词与名词形式。

items.example: It names the act of sending out energy.
items.exampleCN: 它命名发出能量的行为。

items.example: The noun covers both the process and what is emitted.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指过程也指被发出的东西。

items.example: The compound narrows the mass noun to a countable particle.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把不可数的总称收窄为可数的粒子。

definition_en: describing an animal or person that consumes both plant and animal material, or more broadly one with very wide tastes

senses.title: Eating both diets
senses.titleCN: 杂食性：植物与动物性食物兼食
senses.definition: describing an animal that eats both plant and animal material in substantial amounts
senses.definitionCN: 描述大量食用植物与动物性材料两者的动物
senses.example: The omnivorous diet of the fox includes fruit, insects and small mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 狐狸的杂食食谱包括果实、昆虫与小型哺乳动物。
senses.why: The adjective marks the mixed-diet class, which is neither herbivorous nor carnivorous.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出混合食性类别，既非植食也非食肉。

senses.title: Bears and other switch eaters
senses.definition: describing animals such as bears that shift between plant and animal foods as seasons change
senses.definitionCN: 描述熊这类随季节在植物性与动物性食物之间切换的动物
senses.example: Omnivorous bears gain weight on berries before the salmon run.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食的熊在鲑鱼洄游前靠浆果增重。
senses.why: Seasonal switching is the practical advantage of the class: the animal is never stuck with one failing food.
senses.whyCN: 季节切换是这一类的实际优势：动物不会困在单一失败的食物上。

senses.title: Omnivorous birds
senses.titleCN: 杂食鸟类：谷物、昆虫与腐肉都吃
senses.definition: describing birds that take seeds, fruit, insects, eggs or carrion depending on opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 描述视机会取食种子、果实、昆虫、卵或腐肉的鸟类
senses.example: Omnivorous birds adapt quickly when a crop fails.
senses.exampleCN: 作物歉收时，杂食鸟类能迅速适应。
senses.why: Flight lets birds sample many patches, which makes a mixed diet especially efficient.
senses.whyCN: 飞行让鸟类能采样许多斑块，因此混合食性尤其高效。

senses.title: Omnivorous insects
senses.titleCN: 杂食昆虫：既取食植物也取食动物
senses.definition: describing insects that feed on plant tissue and on other animals or carrion
senses.definitionCN: 描述既取食植物组织、也取食其他动物或腐肉的昆虫
senses.example: Omnivorous ants scavenge seeds, insects and dead vertebrates.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食蚂蚁取食种子、昆虫与死亡脊椎动物。
senses.why: Many ants are the clearest examples, because a colony can exploit several food channels at once.
senses.whyCN: 许多蚂蚁是最清楚的例子，因为一个蚁群能同时利用多条食物通道。

senses.title: The human mixed diet
senses.titleCN: 人类混合饮食：谷物与肉并用
senses.definition: describing the human species' capacity to live on a combination of plant and animal foods
senses.definitionCN: 描述人类物种靠植物与动物性食物组合生活的能力
senses.example: Human beings are omnivorous and can survive on many different food mixes.
senses.exampleCN: 人类是杂食性的，能靠许多不同的食物组合生存。
senses.why: The adjective is used at species level in nutrition, describing a capacity rather than a recommended diet.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在营养学中用于物种层面，描述一种能力，而不是推荐食谱。

senses.title: An omnivorous reader
senses.titleCN: 什么书都读的人：阅读范围极广
senses.definition: figuratively describing a person who reads widely across genres, subjects and levels of difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述跨越体裁、主题与难度广泛阅读的人
senses.example: She is an omnivorous reader who moves from biology to detective novels.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个什么书都读的人，从生物学读到侦探小说。
senses.why: The dietary metaphor turns reading into eating: the reader consumes every kind of text.
senses.whyCN: 饮食比喻把阅读变成进食：读者消耗各种文本。

senses.title: Omnivorous curiosity
senses.titleCN: 无所不包的求知欲：什么都想了解
senses.definition: figuratively describing an appetite for knowledge that ranges across unrelated fields
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述横跨不相关领域的求知欲望
senses.example: His omnivorous curiosity led him from fossils to finance.
senses.exampleCN: 他无所不包的求知欲把他从化石带到金融。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from texts to questions, where the 'food' is any subject at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从文本扩展到问题，这里的「食物」可以是任何主题。

senses.title: Cultural and media omnivorousness
senses.titleCN: 文化杂食：品味与平台都不设限
senses.definition: in sociology and media studies, describing a taste or usage pattern that crosses highbrow, popular and multiple platforms
senses.definitionCN: 社会学与媒介研究中描述跨越高雅、通俗与多种平台的品味或使用模式
senses.example: The study found an omnivorous pattern of news consumption across print, video and social media.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现了一种跨纸媒、视频与社交媒体的杂食型新闻消费模式。
senses.why: The adjective has become a technical term for boundary-crossing, not merely for eating everything.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词已成为描述跨界的技术术语，不再只是「什么都吃」。

intro.en: Omnivorous is a scientific Latin adjective from omnis 'all' and vorare 'devour', older than the English noun omnivore.
intro.cn: omnivorous 是科学拉丁语形容词，由 omnis「全部」与 vorare「吞食」构成，比英语名词 omnivore 更早。

items.en: Omnis meant all or every, and its prefix form omni- spread into words about power, knowledge and transport.
items.cn: omnis 意为全部、每个，其前缀形式 omni- 扩散到关于权力、知识与交通的词中。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour, the eating verb shared with herbivorous and carnivorous.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食，与 herbivorous、carnivorous 共用的吃的动词。

items.en: Omnivorus was the adjective for a mixed diet in modern scientific Latin. Its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: omnivorus 是近代科学拉丁语中表示混合食性的形容词；确切首用存疑。

items.en: English omnivorous is recorded in the seventeenth century and was soon used figuratively for broad reading. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 omnivorous 见于 17 世纪，很快被比喻用于广泛阅读；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: Sociology and media studies turned omnivorous into a term for crossing cultural and platform boundaries in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，社会学与媒介研究把 omnivorous 变成描述跨越文化与平台边界的术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vorous ending; the near-meaning group separates mixed diet from wide interest and technical breadth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vorous 结尾；近义组区分混合食性、广泛兴趣与技术性广度。

entries.definition: The animal or person itself. It is a count noun, so a bear is an omnivore with an omnivorous diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物或人本身。它是可数名词，因此熊是 omnivore，其食谱是 omnivorous。

entries.definition: Describes a plant-only diet. The stem herba- replaces omni- and reverses the class.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纯植食。词干 herba- 替换 omni-，类别随之相反。

entries.definition: Describes a flesh-only diet. The stem caro- replaces omni-, and the diet narrows.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纯肉食。词干 caro- 替换 omni-，食性随之收窄。

entries.definition: A species or person that uses many resources. It is broader than omnivorous, which is specifically about food.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用多种资源的物种或人。它比 omnivorous 更宽，后者专指食物。

entries.definition: Describes tastes drawn from many sources. It matches the figurative sense of omnivorous but is used of style and choice, not diet.
entries.definitionCN: 描述从多种来源汲取的品味。它对应 omnivorous 的比喻义，但用于风格与选择，而非食性。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for feeding on many kinds of food, mostly used of insects. It overlaps with omnivorous but belongs to entomology.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指取食多种食物，多用于昆虫。它与 omnivorous 重叠，但属昆虫学用语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: omni 'all' + -vorous 'eating': eating everything.
normal.cn: omni「全部」+ -vorous「吃……的」：什么都吃。

normal.en: Typical phrases: omnivorous animal, omnivorous diet, omnivorous reader, omnivorous curiosity.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：杂食动物、杂食食谱、什么书都读的人、无所不包的求知欲。

normal.en: The family runs omnivore, omnivory, omnibus and omni- words such as omnipotent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 omnivore、omnivory、omnibus，以及 omnipotent 这类 omni- 词。

normal.en: Swap the stem to change the class: omni-, herbi-, carni-.
normal.cn: 换词干就换类别：omni-、herbi-、carni-。

normal.en: In sociology, omnivorous means boundary-crossing taste, not literal eating.
normal.cn: 在社会学中，omnivorous 指跨界的品味，而非字面进食。

abstract.en: Picture one table holding grain, berries, fish and insects, with a fork reaching everywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌上摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，叉子伸向每一处。

abstract.en: Picture a reader with a biology paper and a detective novel open at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者同时摊开一篇生物学论文和一本侦探小说。

abstract.en: Picture one person reading news in print, on video and on a phone before noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在中午前就从纸媒、视频与手机上读新闻。

examples.en: The omnivorous bear moves from berries to salmon as autumn arrives.
examples.cn: 秋天到来时，这只杂食的熊从浆果转向鲑鱼。

examples.en: Omnivorous ants exploit both seeds and dead insects.
examples.cn: 杂食蚂蚁既利用种子也利用死昆虫。

examples.en: Her omnivorous reading made her hard to surprise in conversation.
examples.cn: 她什么书都读，交谈时很难被难住。

dict_mnemonic.text: omnivore（杂食动物）+ ous（……的）→ 杂食的 → omnivorous

root: 拉丁 omnis「全部」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 omnivorus「各类食物都吃的」→ 英语 omnivorous。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to diet, seasonal switching, birds, insects, human capacity, reading, curiosity and cultural breadth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于食性、季节切换、鸟类、昆虫、人类能力、阅读、求知欲与文化广度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table holding grain, berries, fish and insects, reached from every side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌上摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，四面都能取用。

branches.en: DIET: mixed eating is the base, and seasonal switching is its practical payoff.
branches.cn: 食性：混合取食是基本义，季节切换是它的实际收益。

branches.en: ANIMALS: birds and insects show the class across very different body plans.
branches.cn: 动物：鸟类与昆虫展示了这一类在差异极大的体型中的表现。

branches.en: HUMANS: the adjective describes a species-level capacity, not a menu plan.
branches.cn: 人类：这个形容词描述物种层面的能力，而非一份菜单。

branches.en: METAPHOR: reading and curiosity become forms of eating.
branches.cn: 比喻：阅读与求知欲变成进食的形式。

branches.en: TECHNICAL: sociology uses the word for taste that crosses every boundary.
branches.cn: 技术用法：社会学用这个词描述跨越一切边界的品味。

intro.en: Omnivorous is the adjective branch of the 'all-eating' family, and omni- is one of the most transparent prefixes in English.
intro.cn: omnivorous 是「什么都吃」词族的形容词支，omni- 是英语中最透明的前缀之一。

latinIntro.en: Omnis means all, vorare means devour, and -vorus is the scientific adjective ending used across diet words.
latinIntro.cn: omnis 意为全部，vorare 意为吞食，-vorus 是各类食性词共用的科学形容词词尾。

items.meaningCN: 什么都吃的；兴趣广泛的
items.example: The omnivorous fish takes plants and larvae.
items.exampleCN: 这种杂食鱼既吃植物也吃幼虫。

items.example: The omnivore samples every food patch.
items.exampleCN: 这只杂食动物尝试每一处食物斑块。

items.example: Omnivory is common among ants.
items.exampleCN: 杂食性在蚂蚁中很常见。

items.example: Omni- also forms omnipotent and omniscient.
items.exampleCN: omni- 还构成 omnipotent 与 omniscient。

items.example: The omnibus edition collects all four novels.
items.exampleCN: 合集版收录了全部四部小说。

items.example: Herbivorous animals have fermentation chambers.
items.exampleCN: 植食动物有发酵腔。

items.example: Carnivorous animals have shearing teeth.
items.exampleCN: 食肉动物有剪切齿。

items.example: Omnivorous species are often habitat generalists.
items.exampleCN: 杂食物种常常也是生境广适种。

items.example: The exhibit is eclectic in style.
items.exampleCN: 这个展览风格驳杂。

definition_en: to say or show what you think or feel, or to press liquid out of something
core_image: 手一压，汁水从果子里出来，话从心里出来，两件事是同一个动作
scene: 早餐店里，店主把刚榨好的橙汁递给客人，说： We express the oranges fresh every morning.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「榨出、压出汁液」（第 3 个义项：用压力把汁液挤出）；句意为这家店每天早上现榨橙子。

senses.title: Say what one thinks or feels
senses.titleCN: 说出自己的想法或感受
senses.definition: to put thoughts or feelings into words
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或感受用词语说出来
senses.example: He expressed his doubts politely but clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有礼而清楚地表达了自己的疑虑。
senses.why: The oldest image is pressing something out, and a thought pressed out through the mouth becomes speech.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是把东西压出来，而想法从嘴里被压出就成了言语。

senses.title: Show feeling through art or action
senses.titleCN: 通过艺术或行为表现情感
senses.definition: to show a feeling or idea through a work, gesture or act rather than a statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过作品、姿态或行为而不是陈述来显示情感或观点
senses.example: The mural expresses the community's grief.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画表达了社区的悲伤。
senses.why: The channel need not be words; anything that lets an inner state come out can carry the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 渠道不必是词语；任何能让内在状态出来的东西都能承载同一个动词。

senses.title: Press juice or oil out
senses.definition: to squeeze liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用压力从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体
senses.example: The press expresses oil from the seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子里榨出油。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning, still alive in food processing and perfumery.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面意义，在食品加工与香料制作中仍然活着。

senses.title: A fast train
senses.definition: a train that makes few stops and travels quickly
senses.definitionCN: 停站少、运行速度快的列车
senses.example: They caught the night express to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搭上了开往海岸的夜间特快。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century railways borrowed the word to mean a service that presses straight through without delays.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的铁路借用这个词，指一路直推、不作耽搁的服务。

senses.title: Fast delivery service
senses.definition: a service that sends letters or parcels quickly and directly
senses.definitionCN: 快速直接地寄送信件或包裹的服务
senses.example: The package went by express and arrived next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹走快递，第二天早上就到了。
senses.why: The same idea of direct speed moved from trains to mail and parcels.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「直达速度」从列车移到了邮件与包裹。

senses.title: Clearly stated and deliberate
senses.titleCN: 明确说出的；特意如此的
senses.definition: stated openly and with a clear purpose, rather than implied
senses.definitionCN: 公开说明且目的清楚，而非暗示的
senses.example: She came with the express purpose of resigning.
senses.exampleCN: 她来的明确目的就是辞职。
senses.why: Something expressly set out is pressed into clear view, so the adjective came to mean explicit.
senses.whyCN: 被明确摆出来的东西是被压进清晰视野的，因此这个形容词引申为「明确的」。

senses.title: Represent by symbols
senses.definition: to represent a value, relation or idea in symbols or a formula
senses.definitionCN: 用符号或公式表示一个值、关系或观点
senses.example: Express the ratio as a fraction in lowest terms.
senses.exampleCN: 把这个比表示成最简分数。
senses.why: Mathematics presses an abstract relation into visible symbols, continuing the same outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 数学把抽象关系压进可见符号，延续同一个向外的动作。

senses.title: Cause a gene to produce a product
senses.definition: in biology, to make the information in a gene produce a working molecule
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，使基因中的信息产生可用的分子
senses.example: These cells express the protein at high levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞高水平地表达这种蛋白质。
senses.why: A gene's instructions are pressed out into the cell as a product, which is why the same verb serves biology.
senses.whyCN: 基因的指令被压出到细胞里成为产物，因此同一个动词也服务于生物学。

intro.en: Express comes through Old French from Latin exprimere 'to press out, represent', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: express 经古法语来自拉丁语 exprimere「压出、表现」，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere 'to press' is the physical core. Its deeper origin is not established, and the root form often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere「压」是物理核心。其更深来源未得到证明，常为它提出的词根形式属于重构。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere gave exprimere 'to squeeze out'; the verb then acquired the mental sense 'to represent, portray, utter'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 得到 exprimere「挤出」；这个动词随后获得「表现、描绘、说出」的心理意义。

items.en: Old French espresser and expresser carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century with both the physical and the representational senses.
items.cn: 古法语 espresser 与 expresser 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，同时带有物理义与表现义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century a special messenger or dispatch was called an express; railways extended the label to fast trains in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，专门的信使或急件被称为 express；铁路在十九世纪把这个标签扩展到快车。

items.en: The adjective meaning 'clearly stated' developed in the sixteenth century from the idea of something expressly set out.
items.cn: 表示「明确说出」的形容词义在十六世纪发展出来，来自「被特意摆出来」的想法。

items.en: Source uncertain: exact dates of the railway and mail senses vary by region, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：铁路义与邮件义的确切年代因地区而异，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same or neighbouring roots; group two holds near synonyms for the core act of saying or showing.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根或邻近词根的外形相近词；第二组是「说」与「显示」这一核心动作的近义词。

entries.definition: Italian borrowed the same Latin verb for coffee pressed out under steam, so the coffee and the English verb share a root.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语借用了同一个拉丁动词，指用蒸汽压出的咖啡，因此这种咖啡与英语动词同根。

entries.definition: With 'in' rather than 'out': to press a mark or feeling into someone's mind rather than to bring something out.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：把印记或感受压进某人心里，而不是把东西带出来。

entries.definition: It looks like a sibling, but its root means 'to drive', not 'to press'; it means to force someone or something out.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像同族词，其实词根意为「驱赶」而非「压」；意思是把某人或某物赶出去。

entries.definition: It shares the 'out' prefix but its root means 'to draw or pull'; extraction pulls something out rather than pressing it.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带「向外」前缀，但词根意为「拉、抽」；提取是拉出某物，而不是压出。

entries.definition: To carry an idea across to someone; it stresses successful transfer, while express stresses the outward act.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法传递给别人；强调成功送达，而 express 强调向外的动作。

entries.definition: To say something clearly and formally; express is broader and can cover art, gestures and formulas.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而正式地说出；express 更宽，可涵盖艺术、姿态与公式。

entries.definition: A formal verb for producing sounds or words; it has no physical squeezing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指发出声音或词语的正式动词；没有物理上的挤压义。

entries.definition: To express an idea clearly and in an organized way; it adds the idea of clear structure.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而有条理地表达想法；多出「结构清晰」这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing image, the prefix contrast, the transport sense and the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：压出意象、前缀对比、交通义与同族词。

normal.en: The root means 'press out': juice is expressed from fruit, words from a mind.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压出」：从果子里压出汁，从心里压出话。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing is express, inward pressing is impress.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压是「表达」，向内压是「给人印象」。

normal.en: Transport pair: an express train and express mail both move directly and quickly.
normal.cn: 交通配对：特快列车与快递都直达而迅速。

normal.en: The adjective with purpose means explicit, as in an express purpose.
normal.cn: 与「目的」一词连用的形容词义表示「明确的」，如明确目的。

normal.en: The family runs express, expression, expressive and expressly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括动词、名词、形容词与副词四种形式。

abstract.en: Picture an orange and a sentence both being squeezed by the same hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙子和一句话被同一只手挤压。

abstract.en: Picture a train that never stops until it reaches the coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车一路不停，直到抵达海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a thought packed into a parcel and sent overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法被装进包裹，连夜寄出。

examples.en: She expressed her thanks with a small hand-written note.
examples.cn: 她用一张手写的小纸条表达了感谢。

examples.en: The factory expresses oil from locally grown seeds.
examples.cn: 这家工厂用当地种植的种子榨油。

examples.en: The express leaves the city at six and reaches the border by noon.
examples.cn: 特快列车六点离城，中午前到达边境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外压」——把话压出来是说，把汁压出来是榨 → 表达、榨出

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」；premere 更深来源不确定，相关词根形式为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pressure: words out of a mind, feeling out through art, juice out of fruit, speed out of a schedule, clarity out of a statement, symbols out of a relation and a product out of a gene.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一股压力展开：从心里压出话语、通过艺术压出情感、从果子压出汁液、从时刻表压出速度、从陈述压出明确、从关系压出符号、从基因压出产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand presses, and what was inside comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：手一压，里面的东西就出来了。

branches.en: SAY AND SHOW: words and art are two outlets for the same inner pressure.
branches.cn: 说与显：词语与艺术是同一股内在压力的两个出口。

branches.en: LIQUID OUT: the literal squeeze that keeps the root meaning alive.
branches.cn: 汁液出来：字面上的挤压，让词根意义继续活着。

branches.en: DIRECT SPEED: a train and a parcel service both press straight through without delay.
branches.cn: 直达速度：列车与包裹服务都一路直推、不作耽搁。

branches.en: PRESSED INTO CLARITY: something expressly set out cannot be mistaken for an implication.
branches.cn: 压成清晰：特意摆出来的东西不会被误当成暗示。

branches.en: SYMBOL AND CELL: a formula and a gene both make an inner relation or instruction visible and active.
branches.cn: 符号与细胞：公式与基因都让内在关系或指令变得可见并发挥作用。

intro.en: Express is a Latin verb of pressing, and its parts also build nouns, adjectives and adverbs for showing and squeezing.
intro.cn: express 是一个表示「压」的拉丁动词，其部件还构成表示「表现」与「挤压」的名词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- 'out' and premere 'to press' form exprimere; the noun expressio and the adjective expressus extend the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成 exprimere；名词 expressio 与形容词 expressus 延续同一词族。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作送向外面。

items.example: The root names the force behind the action.

items.example: Her expression showed relief.

items.example: The letter was warm and expressive.

items.example: The rules expressly forbid the practice.

items.structure: Italian espresso, from the same Latin verb

items.exampleCN: 咖啡师压出一小杯浓缩咖啡。

items.meaning: to press a mark or feeling in
items.example: The speech impressed the audience.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲给听众留下了深刻印象。

definition_zh: 白蚁；（喻）从内部慢慢蛀空组织的人或事物
definition_en: a pale, soft-bodied social insect that feeds on wood and lives in colonies with distinct castes
core_image: 一块外表完好的木板被撬开，里面是无数细小管道，像被谁用针一层层掏空，只剩一层薄壳
scene: 老房子的地板踩上去还是硬的，可撬开一角，底下已经全是细土一样的碎渣。 One termite is harmless, but a colony can hollow a beam without touching its surface.
sceneCN: 这里 termite 指「白蚁」（第 1 个义项：体色浅、体软、蛀食木材的群居昆虫）；句意为一只白蚁无害，但一个蚁群能在不碰表面的情况下把梁掏空。

白蚁的；由白蚁引起的
