senses.title: The pale wood-eating social insect
senses.titleCN: 浅色、蛀食木材的群居昆虫
senses.definition: a soft-bodied, usually pale insect of the cockroach lineage that lives in colonies and feeds mainly on wood
senses.definitionCN: 体软、通常色浅、属蟑螂谱系、群居并以木材为主食的昆虫
senses.example: One termite is harmless, but a colony can hollow a beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一只白蚁无害，但一个蚁群能把梁掏空。
senses.why: the word names the animal, and the whole vocabulary of damage, mounds and castes is built outward from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名动物，关于损坏、蚁丘与品级的整套词汇都由它向外生长出来。

senses.title: The colony with its castes
senses.definition: the organised society of workers, soldiers and reproductives living in one nest
senses.definitionCN: 在同一巢中生活的工蚁、兵蚁与繁殖个体组成的有组织社会
senses.example: The termite colony was three metres deep and twenty years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这个白蚁群深达三米，已有二十年。
senses.why: because individuals are almost never seen alone, the singular often stands for the whole society.
senses.whyCN: 因为个体几乎从不单独出现，单数常代指整个社会。

senses.title: A named ecological type
senses.definition: a kind identified by habit, such as subterranean, drywood or mound-building termites
senses.definitionCN: 按习性区分的类型，如地下白蚁、干木白蚁、筑丘白蚁
senses.example: Drywood termites need no contact with soil at all.
senses.exampleCN: 干木白蚁完全不需要接触土壤。
senses.why: types are distinguished by where they live, so a qualifier carries the whole difference.
senses.whyCN: 类型由栖息处区分，因此一个限定语承担了全部差别。

senses.title: A destroyer of timber in buildings
senses.definition: the species regarded as a structural pest because it consumes wood from the inside
senses.definitionCN: 因从内部吃空木材而被视为结构害虫的物种
senses.example: Termite damage went unnoticed until the floor sagged.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁的损坏直到地板下沉才被发现。
senses.why: the damage is described by its agent because the insect leaves a hollow shell rather than a visible hole.
senses.whyCN: 损坏由施害者来描述，因为昆虫留下的是空壳而不是明显的洞。

senses.title: A decomposer of dead wood
senses.definition: the ecological role of breaking down fallen timber and returning nutrients to the soil
senses.definitionCN: 分解倒木、把养分归还土壤的生态角色
senses.example: Termites clear dead wood faster than fungi in dry forests.
senses.exampleCN: 在干燥森林里，白蚁分解枯木比真菌更快。
senses.why: the same activity that ruins a house recycles a forest, so the word carries both judgements.
senses.whyCN: 毁屋与还林是同一种活动，因此这个词同时承载两种判断。

senses.title: A subject for symbiosis research
senses.definition: the insect as a host whose gut microbes digest wood, studied as a model of symbiosis
senses.definitionCN: 肠道微生物帮它消化木材，因而作为共生模型被研究的昆虫
senses.example: The termite depends on microbes it passes to its young.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁依赖它传给后代的微生物。
senses.why: a striking biological dependency makes the animal a research system, and the name stands for the system.
senses.whyCN: 一种显著的生物依赖使这种动物成为研究体系，其名称代表这个体系。

senses.title: A builder of ventilated mounds
senses.titleCN: 建造通风蚁丘的建筑者
senses.definition: the mound-building species whose structures regulate heat and gas exchange
senses.definitionCN: 所筑结构能调节热量与气体交换的筑丘物种
senses.example: The termite mound keeps a steady temperature through the day.
senses.exampleCN: 白蚁丘昼夜保持稳定温度。
senses.why: architecture is attributed to a builder, so the insect's name travels to the structure it makes.
senses.whyCN: 建筑被归给建造者，因此昆虫之名也移向它所造的结构。

senses.title: Figurative: something hollowing from within
senses.definition: figurative, a person or institution that undermines a group secretly and gradually
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指暗中、逐步蛀空某个群体的人或机构
senses.example: The report called the smuggling network a termite in the customs service.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把走私网络称作海关内部的白蚁。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the hidden, internal, gradual hollowing, which is exactly what the insect does.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留隐蔽、内部、渐进的掏空，而这正是这种昆虫所做的事。

intro.en: Termite is a late eighteenth-century learned word from Latin termes, the name for a woodworm; its earlier English name was the misleading white ant.
intro.cn: termite 是 18 世纪后期的学术词，出自拉丁 termes「木蠹虫」；其较早英语名是易致误解的 white ant。

items.en: Latin termes named a woodworm or a gnawing insect, and English naturalists revived it for the tropical wood-eating insect.
items.cn: 拉丁 termes 指木蠹虫或蛀咬的昆虫，英语博物学家把它复活用于热带蛀木昆虫。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the origin of Latin termes itself is unresolved; a link to a verb for gnawing has been suggested, but the form given for it is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：拉丁 termes 本身的来源无定论；与某个表示「啃咬」的动词的联系属提议，且所给形式为重构。

items.en: The older English name white ant treated the insect as a pale ant, a mistake that modern classification has corrected.
items.cn: 较早的英语名 white ant 把它当作浅色的蚂蚁，这一错误已被现代分类纠正。

items.en: Termites are now placed with cockroaches rather than with ants, a result of twentieth-century anatomical and molecular work.
items.cn: 白蚁现被归入蟑螂一类而非蚂蚁，这是 20 世纪解剖与分子研究的结果。

items.en: As timber construction spread, the word became a household word for structural damage and for the inspection trade.
items.cn: 随着木结构建筑普及，这个词成为关于结构损坏与检查行业的日常词。

items.en: The image of hidden internal hollowing produced the political metaphor of a termite inside an institution.
items.cn: 隐蔽内部掏空的意象产生了「机构内部白蚁」的政治比喻。

note.en: Group one separates termite from the insects it is historically confused with; group two separates the animal from its products and its metaphors.
note.cn: 第一组区分 termite 与其历史上易混的昆虫；第二组区分动物本身与其产物、比喻。

entries.definition: The insect once called a white ant; ants are darker, have a narrow waist and belong to a different order.
entries.definitionCN: 曾被叫作白蚁的昆虫；蚂蚁颜色更深、腰细，且属另一目。

entries.definition: An old English name for the termite, still met in older books; the insect is neither white nor an ant.
entries.definitionCN: 白蚁的旧英语名，仍见于旧书；它既不白也不是蚂蚁。

entries.definition: The nest or mound itself, not the insect; the -arium suffix marks a place.
entries.definitionCN: 巢或丘本身，而非昆虫；-arium 后缀标记场所。

entries.definition: A product that kills termites, built with the -cide suffix of killing.
entries.definitionCN: 杀白蚁的产品，由表「杀」的 -cide 后缀构成。

entries.definition: Woodworm names the larvae of wood-boring beetles; Latin termes covered similar gnawers before it was fixed to termites.
entries.definitionCN: woodworm 指蛀木甲虫的幼虫；拉丁 termes 在被固定指白蚁前也涵盖类似的蛀虫。

entries.definition: A carpenter ant excavates galleries in wood but does not eat it; a termite actually digests the wood.
entries.definitionCN: 木匠蚁在木中挖道但不吃木；白蚁则真正消化木材。

entries.definition: Borer names any animal that drills into wood or stems; termite names a particular social insect.
entries.definitionCN: borer 指任何钻入木材或茎的动物；termite 指特定的社会性昆虫。

entries.definition: Decomposer is a functional role in a food web; termite is the organism that fills it in dry forests.
entries.definitionCN: decomposer 是食物网中的功能角色；白蚁是在干燥森林中承担该角色的生物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source, the real misnomer and real trade terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁来源、真实误称与真实行业用语。

normal.en: Latin termes meant a woodworm, and English took it for the tropical wood-eater.
normal.cn: 拉丁 termes 指木蠹虫，英语用它指热带的蛀木者。

normal.en: The old name white ant is a double mistake: not white, not an ant.
normal.cn: 旧名 white ant 是双重错误：既不白，也不是蚂蚁。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: termite damage, termite mound, termite inspection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：白蚁损坏、白蚁丘、白蚁检查。

normal.en: Termites are now classified with cockroaches, not with ants.
normal.cn: 白蚁现被归入蟑螂一类，而非蚂蚁。

normal.en: Termites digest wood with microbes in their gut, a standard case of symbiosis.
normal.cn: 白蚁靠肠道微生物消化木材，是共生的标准案例。

abstract.en: Picture a beam that sounds solid when tapped and is dust inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一根梁，敲起来是实的，里面却是粉。

abstract.en: Picture a city of narrow corridors built without a single window.
abstract.cn: 想象一座全是窄走廊、没有一扇窗的城市。

abstract.en: Picture a flaw that eats an organisation while its reports look clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一个缺陷在吞噬机构，而报告看起来一切正常。

examples.en: Termites reached the sill through a mud tube built in the dark.
examples.cn: 白蚁沿着在暗处筑成的泥管到达了门槛。

examples.en: The mound was opened and the termites were gone within an hour.
examples.cn: 蚁丘被打开后，白蚁一小时内就撤空了。

examples.en: Inspectors look for termites before any sale of the house.
examples.cn: 房屋出售前，检查人员会找白蚁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ter（土）+ mite」——在土里做巢、把木头蛀成粉的虫 → 白蚁

root: 拉丁 termes「木蠹虫、蛀虫」，英语在 18 世纪后期借入指白蚁；拉丁词本身的更深来源不确定，与「啃咬」动词的联系仅为重构性提议。旧英语名 white ant 属误称。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hidden hollowing: a pale insect eats wood from inside, and the word then names the colony, a type, a structural pest, a decomposer, a symbiosis model, a mound builder, and finally a person who undermines from within.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种隐蔽的掏空展开：浅色昆虫从内部吃木；词语随后指群体、类型、结构害虫、分解者、共生模型、筑丘者，最后指从内部蛀空的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam that looks intact until the shell is lifted and only dust remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根看似完好的梁，撬开薄壳后只剩粉末。

branches.en: INSECT AND SOCIETY: one animal, then the caste system it never leaves.
branches.cn: 昆虫与社会：一只动物，然后是它从不脱离的品级体系。

branches.en: HABIT TYPES: subterranean, drywood and mound builders are one word plus a qualifier.
branches.cn: 习性命型：地下、干木、筑丘都是一个词加限定语。

branches.en: TWO VERDICTS: destroyer of a building, restorer of a forest.
branches.cn: 两种裁断：建筑的破坏者，森林的恢复者。

branches.en: RESEARCH AND ARCHITECTURE: the gut microbes and the ventilated mound.
branches.cn: 研究与建筑：肠道微生物与通风的蚁丘。

branches.en: HIDDEN CORROSION: the insect becomes an accusation about institutions.
branches.cn: 隐蔽腐蚀：昆虫变成对机构的指控。

intro.en: Termite is a learned Latin borrowing with no English prefix; its family is built with Latin and Greek suffixes.
intro.cn: termite 是拉丁学术借词，无英语前缀；其词族由拉丁与希腊后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin termes gives termite and termitarium; Greek isopteron 'equal wing' gives the old order name Isoptera.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 termes 提供 termite 与 termitarium；希腊 isopteron「等翅」提供旧目名 Isoptera。

items.example: The Latin word named a wood-eater long before the tropics were studied.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词早在热带被研究之前就指蛀木者。

items.example: The termite builds tubes of mud.
items.exampleCN: 白蚁筑泥管。

items.example: Termites worked through the floor.
items.exampleCN: 白蚁把地板吃穿了。

items.example: The termitarium rose two metres.
items.exampleCN: 白蚁巢高出两米。

items.example: The soil was treated with a termiticide.
items.exampleCN: 土壤用杀白蚁剂处理过。

items.example: The damage was termitic in origin.
items.exampleCN: 这项损坏源自白蚁。

items.example: Isoptera is the older order name for termites.
items.exampleCN: Isoptera 是白蚁的旧目名。

items.example: Isopterology has few specialists.
items.exampleCN: 研究白蚁的专家很少。

items.example: White ant appears only in older texts.
items.exampleCN: white ant 只见于较旧的文本。

definition_zh: 可变性；变异性；变动幅度；（统计）离散程度
definition_en: the quality or degree of being changeable, or the extent to which values differ from one another
core_image: 同一块地的十次收成排成一列，高低差别明显，尺子量出的正是这些差别
scene: 这里指「可变性」。 Rainfall variability makes farming risky in this region.
sceneCN: 这里 variability 指「变动幅度」（第 1 个义项：随时间或个案变化、不稳定）；句意：降水量的变动使该地区的农业风险很大。图中可辨识物件：逐年降水柱状图、干裂的田块、蓄水池。

pos.zh: 可变性；变异性；变动幅度；（统计）离散程度（多为不可数，也可用 variabilities 指多种变异）

senses.title: Changeability
senses.definition: the quality of being changeable
senses.definitionCN: 容易发生变化的性质
senses.example: Rainfall variability makes farming risky in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 降水量的变化使该地区的农业风险很大。
senses.why: Varius in Latin meant 'diverse, spotted, changeable'. The noun -ability turns that quality into a measurable thing: not 'it changes' but 'how much it changes'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 varius 意为「多样的、有斑点的、易变的」。名词后缀 -ability 把这种性质变成可度量之物：不是「它变」，而是「它变得有多少」。

senses.title: Statistical Spread
senses.titleCN: 统计离散：数值彼此差多少
senses.definition: the extent to which values in a set differ from one another
senses.definitionCN: 一组数值之间相互差异的程度
senses.example: The variability of the scores was low, so the class was evenly matched.
senses.exampleCN: 分数的离散程度很低，说明这个班水平相当。
senses.why: Statistics needs a word for difference rather than average. Variability measures how far the members scatter, which is why it pairs with standard deviation and range.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一个词来表示「差异」而不是「平均」；variability 量的是成员分散得多远，因此它与标准差、极差等概念搭配。

senses.title: Biological Variation
senses.titleCN: 生物变异：同种个体间的差异
senses.definition: the range of differences among individuals of a species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种个体之间的差异范围
senses.example: Genetic variability gives a population a chance to survive a new disease.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传变异让一个种群有机会熬过新的疾病。
senses.why: Evolution depends on differences, not on uniformity. Here variability is a resource: the wider the spread, the more likely some member fits a changed world.
senses.whyCN: 演化依赖差异而非整齐划一。此时 variability 是一种资源：分布越宽，越可能有某个成员适应改变了的世界。

senses.title: Climate Fluctuation
senses.definition: the degree to which climate conditions differ from year to year or place to place
senses.definitionCN: 气候条件在年际或地点之间的差异程度
senses.example: Natural variability hides the slower trend for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 自然波动会在数十年里掩盖较慢的趋势。
senses.why: A trend is a direction; variability is the noise around it. Climate science separates the two, because a wet year says nothing about a warming century.
senses.whyCN: 趋势是方向，变率是围绕方向的噪声。气候科学要把两者分开，因为一个多雨的年份说明不了整个世纪在变暖。

senses.title: Measurement Noise
senses.titleCN: 测量波动：同一对象反复测出的差别
senses.definition: the differences between repeated measurements of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 对同一对象反复测量所得结果之间的差异
senses.example: The variability between the three readings came from the old balance.
senses.exampleCN: 三次读数的波动来自那台旧天平。
senses.why: Instruments never repeat perfectly. The noun names that scatter, and a low value is a sign of a trustworthy method rather than of a stable world.
senses.whyCN: 仪器从不完美重复；这个名词命名的正是那种分散，而数值低说明方法可信，并不说明世界稳定。

senses.title: Beat-to-Beat Range
senses.titleCN: 心率变异性：逐次心跳的间隔差
senses.definition: the variation in the time between heartbeats
senses.definitionCN: 心跳之间时间间隔的变化
senses.example: High heart rate variability is usually a sign of a healthy nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 较高的心率变异性通常意味着神经系统健康。
senses.why: Medicine uses the statistical sense on a living signal. A perfectly regular pulse can be a warning, so variability here is not noise but information.
senses.whyCN: 医学把统计义用在活体信号上；完全规律的脉搏反而可能是警讯，因此这里的变异性不是噪声，而是信息。

senses.title: Genetic Range
senses.titleCN: 遗传变异度：基因库里的多样性
senses.definition: the amount of genetic difference carried within a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体内部所携带的遗传差异总量
senses.example: The island population lost much of its genetic variability.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛屿种群失去了大部分遗传变异。
senses.why: Small populations lose variants by chance. The word then measures a store of options, which conservation biology treats as something to protect.
senses.whyCN: 小种群会因偶然丢失变体；此时这个词量的是选项的储备，保护生物学把它当作需要保护的对象。

senses.title: Inconsistency of Quality
senses.definition: the unevenness of quality or performance over time
senses.definitionCN: 质量或表现在时间上的不均衡
senses.example: Customers complained about the variability of the product.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客抱怨该产品的质量波动。
senses.why: In manufacturing, variability is the enemy of trust: two units of the same model should behave alike. The word shifts from description to a defect to be reduced.
senses.whyCN: 在制造业，变异性是信任的敌人：同一型号的两件产品应当表现一致。此时该词从描述变成一种应当被降低的缺陷。

intro.en: Variability is formed from variable plus -ity, and variable comes from Latin variabilis, from variare 'to change', from varius 'diverse, spotted'. The origin of varius itself is uncertain, and the first English date is only approximate.
intro.cn: variability 由 variable 加 -ity 构成；variable 出自拉丁 variabilis，来自 variare「变化」，而 variare 又来自 varius「多样的、有斑点的」。varius 本身的来源不确定，英语首见年代仅为约数。

items.en: Varius meant 'of various kinds, spotted, mottled, changeable'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: some connect it with a root for 'to weave or vary', but no source is agreed.
items.cn: varius 意为「多种多样的、有斑点的、斑驳的、易变的」。它更深的来源不确定：有人把它与表示「编织、变化」的词根联系起来，但没有公认的来源。此处标注为来源不确定。

items.en: The verb variare meant 'to diversify, to change, to alternate'. It was used for colouring, for altering a plan and for taking turns.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为「使多样、改变、交替」，可用于上色、改变计划，也可指轮流。

items.en: Variabilis meant 'changeable, inconstant'. Latin built it with the suffix -bilis, 'able to be', which English keeps in -able.
items.cn: variabilis 意为「可变的、不恒定的」。拉丁语用后缀 -bilis「能够被……」构成它，英语以 -able 保留了这个后缀。

items.en: English variable appears in the fifteenth century from Old French. Variability followed later, adding -ity to make the quality into a noun. Exact first citations are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 variable 于十五世纪经古法语出现；variability 稍后加上 -ity，把这种性质变成名词。确切的首见书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries variability acquired a technical sense in statistics and biology: the measurable spread of a set of observations. The old idea of changeability became a number.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，variability 在统计学与生物学中获得专门含义：一组观测值可测量的离散程度。古老的「易变」观念由此变成了一个数字。

note.en: The first group separates nouns and adjectives of the same Latin family that are easy to mix. The second holds near-synonyms from statistics and everyday speech.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的名词与形容词；第二组是统计学与日常用语中的近义词。

entries.definition: A particular change or difference, or the act of varying. It counts differences; variability measures how large the differences are.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一具体变化或差异，或变化的行为；它数差异的个数，而 variability 量差异的大小。

entries.definition: In statistics, the average squared deviation; in law, a permission to depart from a rule. It is a precise quantity, not a general quality.
entries.definitionCN: 统计学中指离差平方的平均值；法律中指对规则适用的例外许可。它是精确的量，不是一般的性质。

entries.definition: The adjective 'changeable' or the noun for a quantity that can take different values. The noun names the thing that varies, not the amount of varying.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「易变的」，或指可取不同值的量；该名词命名的是会变的东西，而不是变化的幅度。

entries.definition: An irregular rising and falling, as of prices. It stresses movement up and down rather than the spread of values.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则地上下起伏，如价格；强调上下运动，而不是数值的分散。

entries.definition: A tendency to change or become unbalanced. It carries more risk and less measurement than variability.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于变化或失衡；比 variability 含更多风险意味，更少测量意味。

entries.definition: The presence of many different kinds. It counts variety of types, while variability measures differences within a measure.
entries.definitionCN: 存在许多不同种类；它数类型的多样，而 variability 量同一度量内的差异。

entries.definition: The spreading of values around a centre. It is a technical near-synonym of variability in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 数值围绕中心散布；在统计学中是 variability 的技术性近义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: varius 'varied' + -able 'able to' + -ity: the quality of being able to vary.
normal.cn: varius「多样的」+ -able「能够」+ -ity：能够变化的性质。

normal.en: The family runs vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: climate variability, genetic variability, heart rate variability, measurement variability.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：气候变率、遗传变异度、心率变异性、测量波动。

normal.en: variability is how much things differ; variation is a particular difference.
normal.cn: variability 是差异有多大，variation 是某一处具体的差异。

normal.en: Low variability in a factory is good; high variability in a gene pool is good.
normal.cn: 工厂里变异性低是好事，基因库里变异性高是好事。

abstract.en: Picture a row of ten identical cups, then a row where every cup is a different height.
abstract.cn: 想象一排十只一模一样的杯子，再想象一排每只高度都不同的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a scatter of dots to show how far they wander from the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横放在散乱的点上，用来显示它们离中心有多远。

abstract.en: Picture a heartbeat that is never exactly on time, and a doctor smiling at the irregularity.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗从不准时的心跳，而医生对这种不规则微笑。

examples.en: The study measured the variability of response times across four groups.
examples.cn: 该研究测量了四组反应时间的波动程度。

examples.en: High variability in rainfall forces farmers to store water.
examples.cn: 降水的剧烈变动迫使农民储水。

examples.en: Reducing variability is the first aim of any production line.
examples.cn: 降低波动是任何生产线的首要目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: variable（可变的）+ ility（性质）→ 可变的程度 → 可变性、变异性

root: 拉丁 varius「多样的、有斑点的」（来源不确定）→ variare「变化」→ variabilis「可变的」→ 英语 variable → variability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much something differs: a general quality, a statistical spread, biological difference, climate noise, instrument scatter, heartbeat range, genetic variety and uneven quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「差异有多大」：一般性质、统计离散、生物差异、气候噪声、仪器散布、心跳间隔、遗传多样与质量起伏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of unequal harvests, and a ruler laid across the differences.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排高低不等的收成，一把尺子横放在这些差异之上。

branches.en: QUALITY BECOMES QUANTITY: a vague property of being changeable turns into a measurable spread.
branches.cn: 性质变成数量：模糊的「易变」性质变成了可测量的离散度。

branches.en: VARIATION AS RESOURCE: genetic differences give a population options, and a narrow pool is a risk.
branches.cn: 变异作为资源：遗传差异给种群提供选项，而狭窄的基因库是一种风险。

branches.en: NOISE VERSUS TREND: year-to-year wobble can hide a slow direction for decades.
branches.cn: 噪声与趋势：年际抖动可以在数十年里掩盖缓慢的方向。

branches.en: READING A SIGNAL: in instruments the scatter means error, while in a heartbeat it can mean health.
branches.cn: 读取信号：在仪器上散布意味着误差，在心跳上却可能意味着健康。

branches.en: QUALITY CONTROL: identical products should behave alike, so variability becomes a defect to reduce.
branches.cn: 质量控制：相同产品应当表现一致，因此变异性成为需要降低的缺陷。

intro.en: Variability is a Latin-rooted adjective turned into a quality-noun: a root meaning 'varied', the suffix -able, and the suffix -ity.
intro.cn: variability 是拉丁词根的形容词转化为性质名词：表示「多样」的词根、后缀 -able，以及后缀 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and variare supply vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various and varietas, the ancestor of variety.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 varius 与 variare 衍生 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various，以及 variety 的祖形 varietas。

items.example: Variability in the data was greater than expected.
items.exampleCN: 数据的波动比预期更大。

items.meaning: changeable; a quantity that can vary
items.meaningCN: 易变的；可取不同值的量
items.example: Temperature is the key variable in the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 温度是该实验的关键变量。

items.example: Results vary widely between regions.
items.exampleCN: 各地结果差异很大。

items.meaning: a change; a difference in form
items.example: Slight variation in colour is normal.
items.exampleCN: 颜色的轻微差异是正常的。

items.meaningCN: 差异；离差平方的平均值
items.example: The variance of the sample was small.
items.exampleCN: 样本的方差很小。

items.meaning: a different form of the same thing
items.example: A rare variant appeared in the north.
items.exampleCN: 北方出现了一种罕见的变体。

items.example: The shelf held various tools.
items.exampleCN: 架子上放着各种工具。

items.example: The garden grows a wide variety of herbs.
items.exampleCN: 园子里种着多种香草。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 多样的；有斑点的；易变的（更深来源不确定）

definition_zh: 抵消；补偿；弥补；对冲；偏移；胶印
definition_en: to balance one cost, effect or influence against another so that the net result is reduced
core_image: 天平一端压着涨价账单，另一端放上节省下来的硬币，横梁慢慢回到水平
scene: 运费涨了不少，但仓库搬到近郊后省下的租金正好填上这块。 The savings offset the higher freight cost.
sceneCN: 这里指用省下的钱抵掉多出来的开支（第 1 个义项：抵消成本或开支）；句意为节省的费用抵消了上涨的运费。图中可辨识物件：天平、涨价的账单、一叠硬币。

pos.zh: 抵消；补偿；弥补；对冲
抵消；偏移；胶印

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示进行或性质的后缀构成，义为「抵消；起抵消作用的」
名词复数，义为「各项抵消额；偏移量」
由「碳」与「抵消额」合成的复合词，义为「碳抵消额度」

senses.title: To cancel a cost
senses.definition: to balance an extra cost with a saving elsewhere so that the net charge falls
senses.definitionCN: 用在别处省下的钱抵掉额外开支，使净支出下降
senses.example: The lower rent offset the rise in transport fees.
senses.exampleCN: 更低的租金抵消了运费的上涨。
senses.why: The word pictures one item set against another on a scale, and money is the easiest thing to weigh that way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的画面是把一项放在天平上与另一项对着，而钱最容易被这样称量。

senses.title: To compensate for a loss
senses.definition: to make up for a loss or disadvantage with a gain in another area
senses.definitionCN: 用另一方面的收益补上损失或劣势
senses.example: Higher output offset the loss of two machines.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的产量补偿了两台机器的损失。
senses.why: Compensation is the accounting face of the same balance: what was lost is entered against what was gained.
senses.whyCN: 补偿是同一平衡的会计面孔：失去的与得到的对着记账。

senses.title: To make up for a shortfall
senses.definition: to supply what is missing so that the total reaches the required level
senses.definitionCN: 补上缺少的部分，使总量达到应有水平
senses.example: Extra tutoring offset the gap in her early schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 额外的辅导弥补了她早期教育的缺口。
senses.why: A shortfall is an imbalance on one side, and the verb puts weight on the other side.
senses.whyCN: 缺口是一侧的不平衡，这个动词往另一侧放上重量。

senses.title: To hedge a risk
senses.definition: to arrange a position that moves opposite to a risk so that losses are limited
senses.definitionCN: 安排一个与风险反向的头寸，以限制损失
senses.example: The airline offset its fuel exposure with forward contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司用远期合约对冲燃油敞口。
senses.why: Finance takes the scale literally: two positions are set against each other on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 金融把这个天平照字面使用：两个头寸被有意对着摆。

senses.title: To shift a position
senses.definition: to move an object or a line away from its original centre or alignment
senses.definitionCN: 使物体或线条离开原来的中心或对齐位置
senses.example: The surveyor offset the foundation line by ten centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员把基础线偏移了十厘米。
senses.why: Printing and engineering use offset for a displacement, the same side-by-side picture moved into space.
senses.whyCN: 印刷与工程用这个词表示位移，即同一「错开摆放」的画面移入空间。

senses.title: To balance the books
senses.definition: to enter one amount against another so that the accounts agree
senses.definitionCN: 把一笔金额对着另一笔记账，使账目相符
senses.example: The auditor offset the advance against the final invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 审计员把预付款与最终发票相抵。
senses.why: Accounting formalised the scale into two columns that must come to the same total.
senses.whyCN: 会计把这个天平固定成两栏，两栏最后要合成同一个数。

senses.title: To print by offset
senses.definition: to print from a plate onto a rubber blanket and then onto paper
senses.definitionCN: 先把印版上的图文转到橡皮布，再转到纸上
senses.example: The booklet was offset on coated stock.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子用胶印印在铜版纸上。
senses.why: The printing sense grew from the idea of an indirect transfer, ink being set off onto another surface.
senses.whyCN: 印刷义从「间接转移」长出，油墨被「转印」到另一表面。

senses.title: To neutralise emissions
senses.definition: to remove or balance an amount of carbon or pollution by an equivalent saving elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 用在别处等量的减排来抵消一定量的碳排放或污染
senses.example: The firm offset its flights by funding a forest project.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司通过资助一个森林项目来抵消其航班的排放。
senses.why: Climate policy borrowed the accounting verb and made the two pans visible as emissions and removals.
senses.whyCN: 气候政策借用了这个会计动词，把天平两端的排放与移除摆到明面上。

intro.en: Offset is an English compound of off and set, first meaning to set out or start, later to place one thing against another. The printing sense arrived in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: 这是英语中由 off 与 set 构成的复合词，最初意为「出发、开始」，后来指「把一物对着另一物摆放」；印刷义在十九世纪出现。

items.en: Set goes back to Old English settan, to place or cause to sit, and it supplies the placing half of the compound.
items.cn: set 可追溯到古英语 settan「放置、使坐」，提供这个复合词「摆放」的那一半。

items.en: Off marks separation or away, so offset began as a placing away from the main line.
items.cn: off 标出分离或离开，所以这个词最初指「放在主线之外」。

items.en: The early verb meant to set out on a journey, a sense now carried by set off rather than offset.
items.cn: 早期动词义为「出发上路」，这一义今天由「出发」那一短语承担，而不是本词。

items.en: The accounting and balancing sense developed later; the exact date of that shift is uncertain and is usually given only as the early modern period.
items.cn: 会计与抵消义后来才发展出来；这一转变的确切年代不确定，通常只给近代早期这一约数。

items.en: Offset printing named the transfer of ink from plate to blanket to paper, an indirect set-off.
items.cn: 胶印得名于油墨从印版转到橡皮布再到纸上的间接转印。

items.en: Carbon offset extended the accounting image to emissions, with one pan holding what is released and the other what is removed.
items.cn: 碳抵消把会计画面扩展到排放，一端放释放的量，另一端放移除的量。

note.en: The first group looks close or shares the set root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of compensation.
note.cn: 第一组与「offset」形近或共享 set 词根；第二组是与「补偿」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The present participle and noun for the act of balancing one item against another.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词与名词，指把一项对着另一项抵消。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to start a journey or to trigger something.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，指出发或触发。

entries.definition: The beginning of something, from the same set with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指开端，由同一个表示「放置」的词根配不同前缀。

entries.definition: The machine used in offset printing.
entries.definitionCN: 胶印所用的机器。

entries.definition: A reversal or delay, from set and back rather than set and off.
entries.definitionCN: 指挫折或延误，由表示「放置」的词与表示「向后」的词构成。

entries.definition: To weigh against something with equal force.
entries.definitionCN: 指以相等的力量与之抗衡。

entries.definition: To make up for a loss or a disadvantage.
entries.definitionCN: 指弥补损失或劣势。

entries.definition: To bring two sides into equal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指使两边重量相等。

entries.definition: To cancel the effect of something completely.
entries.definitionCN: 指彻底取消某物的作用。

entries.definition: To supply what is missing, in everyday wording.
entries.definitionCN: 指补上缺少的部分，日常说法。

entries.definition: To protect against a financial risk by an opposite position.
entries.definitionCN: 指用反向头寸防范金融风险。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two halves off and set, the accounting image and the printing trade term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 off 与 set 两个部分、会计的天平画面，以及印刷行业术语。

normal.en: Off means away and set means place, so offset is to place one thing against another.
normal.cn: off 是「离开」，set 是「放置」，所以这个词就是把一物对着另一物放。

normal.en: The past tense does not change: offset, offset, offsetting.
normal.cn: 过去式不变：offset、offset、offsetting。

normal.en: Accounting says to offset an advance against an invoice.
normal.cn: 会计说把预付款与发票相抵。

normal.en: Printers speak of offset printing, where ink is transferred twice.
normal.cn: 印刷行话说胶印，油墨要转印两次。

normal.en: Carbon offset is the modern phrase for balancing emissions with removals.
normal.cn: 碳抵消是用移除量平衡排放量的现代说法。

abstract.en: To offset is to admit that a gain and a loss can sit on the same scale.
abstract.cn: 抵消，就是承认一份得与一份失可以放在同一架天平上。

abstract.en: Nothing is undone by offsetting; the scale simply returns to level.
abstract.cn: 抵消并没有撤销什么，只是让天平回到水平。

abstract.en: Every saving you find is a weight you may later place against a cost you cannot avoid.
abstract.cn: 你找到的每一笔节省，都是日后可以放到无法避免的开支对面的重量。

examples.en: Fuel savings offset the higher purchase price within three years.
examples.cn: 燃油节省在三年内抵消了更高的购价。

examples.en: The charity offsets its office emissions by planting trees.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构通过植树抵消办公排放。

examples.en: The pipe was offset slightly to clear the beam.
examples.cn: 为了避开梁，这根管子被略微偏移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥夫塞特」——天平一端压账单，一端放硬币：抵消、补偿

root: 英语复合词，由表示「离开」的前缀与表示「放置」的古英语动词构成；先指出发，后指抵消与错开摆放；印刷义为十九世纪。抵消义的确切转变年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses put two things on opposite pans: cost, loss, shortfall, risk, position, accounts, print and emissions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把两样东西放到天平两端：成本、损失、缺口、风险、位置、账目、印刷与排放。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bill sits on one pan and a stack of coins on the other until the beam levels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一端压着账单，另一端放上硬币，横梁慢慢回到水平。

branches.en: THE TWO COLUMNS: an extra cost meets a saving, and the books are made to agree.
branches.cn: 两栏相对：额外开支遇上节省，账目被做成相符。

branches.en: THE GAP IS FILLED: a loss or a shortfall is covered from the other side.
branches.cn: 缺口被填：损失或不足由另一端补上。

branches.en: THE RISK IS HEDGED: a position is deliberately placed opposite to a threat.
branches.cn: 风险被对冲：有意把一笔头寸摆在威胁的对面。

senses.title: The Science of Structure
senses.titleCN: 解剖学：研究身体结构的学科
senses.definition: the scientific study of the structure of living bodies
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体结构的科学
senses.example: Anatomy students spend the first term learning every bone of the hand.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖学学生第一学期要学完手部每一块骨头。
senses.why: Greek ana- meant 'up, throughout' and temnein meant 'to cut'. Anatomē was a cutting-up, and the name of the act became the name of the science that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊前缀 ana- 意为「向上、遍及」，temnein 意为「切」。anatomē 就是「切开」，这个动作的名称后来变成了从事该动作的学科名称。

senses.title: Body Structure Itself
senses.titleCN: 身体结构：部件如何安排
senses.definition: the actual structure of a body, its parts and their arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 身体实际的结构、各部分及其排列
senses.example: The dolphin's anatomy shows that its flipper is a modified arm.
senses.exampleCN: 海豚的身体结构表明，它的鳍肢是改造过的手臂。
senses.why: The same noun names the object as well as the study. When a biologist says 'the anatomy of the dolphin', the cutting has become a description of what was found.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指学科也指对象；当生物学家说 the anatomy of the dolphin 时，「切」已经变成了对所见之物的描述。

senses.title: The Act of Dissection
senses.titleCN: 解剖：切开并分离的动作
senses.definition: the act or practice of cutting a body apart to study it
senses.definitionCN: 为研究而把身体切开的动作或做法
senses.example: The anatomy of the specimen took the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 对这份标本的解剖花了一整个下午。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the physical cutting. Modern laboratories may use imaging instead, but the word still remembers the knife.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：实际的切割。现代实验室可能改用成像技术，但这个词仍记得那把刀。

senses.title: Detailed Analysis
senses.titleCN: 剖析：把一个整体拆开来看
senses.definition: a detailed examination of the parts of a thing or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对事物或观念的各个部分所作的细致检查
senses.example: The book is an anatomy of how rumours spread.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对谣言如何传播的一次剖析。
senses.why: The metaphor is exact: to understand a whole, take it apart part by part. Analysts therefore borrow the anatomist's word for structures that are not biological.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻非常贴切：要理解一个整体，就把它一部分一部分拆开。因此分析者借解剖学家的词，用于并非生物的结构。

senses.title: The Human Body
senses.definition: the human body, especially in informal or humorous use
senses.definitionCN: 人的身体，尤用于口语或戏谑
senses.example: He fell and bruised his entire anatomy.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔了一跤，全身都碰伤了。
senses.why: Because anatomy studies the body, the noun can stand for the body itself. The tone is usually light, as if the speaker were looking at the body from outside.
senses.whyCN: 因为解剖学研究身体，这个名词可以代指身体本身；语气通常轻松，仿佛说话者从外部打量这具身体。

senses.title: Plant and Animal Structure
senses.titleCN: 动植物结构：非人体的解剖
senses.definition: the structure of plants or animals studied as a field
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究领域的植物或动物结构
senses.example: Plant anatomy explains why stems bend toward light.
senses.exampleCN: 植物解剖学解释了茎为何向光弯曲。
senses.why: The science is not limited to people. Comparative anatomy compares species, and plant anatomy studies tissues; the same cutting-up logic applies.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学并不限于人。比较解剖学比较各物种，植物解剖学研究组织；「切开来看」的逻辑是一样的。

senses.title: Structure of an Institution
senses.titleCN: 机构的结构：组织如何构成
senses.definition: the internal structure and working parts of an organization or system
senses.definitionCN: 组织或系统的内部结构与运作部件
senses.example: The report examined the anatomy of the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告考察了医疗服务体系的结构。
senses.why: Institutions have parts that can be mapped like organs. The word implies that the parts are interdependent, so a change in one shows up elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 机构有可以像器官一样被描绘的部件；这个词暗示各部件相互依赖，因此改一处就会在别处显现。

senses.title: The Anatomy Course
senses.titleCN: 解剖学课程：作为科目的解剖
senses.definition: the subject or course taught under this name
senses.definitionCN: 以解剖学为名讲授的科目或课程
senses.example: She passed anatomy but failed physiology.
senses.exampleCN: 她解剖学通过了，生理学却没过。
senses.why: In medical schools the science becomes a subject with exams. Names of disciplines often work this way: biology is both a field and a class at nine o'clock.
senses.whyCN: 在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的科目。学科名称常如此运作：biology 既是研究领域，也是九点钟的那堂课。

intro.en: Anatomy comes from Greek anatomē 'a cutting up', from ana- 'up, throughout' and temnein 'to cut'. Latin borrowed it as anatomia, and English took it in the sixteenth century; the exact date is approximate.
intro.cn: anatomy 出自希腊 anatomē「切开」，由 ana-「向上、遍及」与 temnein「切」构成。拉丁语借作 anatomia，英语于十六世纪引入；确切年代为约数。

items.en: Temnein meant 'to cut'. From it came tomos 'a cut' and the adjective -tomos, which survives in English compounds such as appendectomy and lobotomy.
items.cn: temnein 意为「切」，由此产生 tomos「切口」与形容词 -tomos；后者在英语复合词中留存，如 appendectomy（阑尾切除术）、lobotomy（脑叶切断术）。

items.en: The same root produced atomos, 'uncuttable', from a- 'not' plus tomos. Democritus used it for the smallest indivisible piece of matter. Anatomy and atom are therefore opposites built from one verb: one cuts up, the other cannot be cut.
items.cn: 同一词根产生 atomos「不可切的」，由 a-「不」加 tomos 构成；德谟克利特用它指不可再分的最小物质。因此 anatomy 与 atom 是由同一个动词造出的反义对：一个切开，一个不可切。

items.en: Anatomē meant 'a cutting up, dissection'. Greek medicine used it for the procedure of opening a body to learn its parts, not for the parts themselves.
items.cn: anatomē 意为「切开、解剖」。希腊医学用它指打开身体以了解其部件的操作，而不是指部件本身。

items.en: Latin anatomia kept both the act and the science. Medieval and Renaissance anatomists added the sense 'the structure so revealed', which English inherited.
items.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 同时保留行为与学科两义；中世纪与文艺复兴时期的解剖学家又添上「由此揭示的结构」这一含义，英语继承了它。

items.en: From the seventeenth century English extended anatomy to the parts of anything, from a poem to a government. The metaphor survives because every whole can be taken apart.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，英语把 anatomy 扩展到任何事物的部件，从一首诗到一个政府。这个比喻之所以存活，是因为任何整体都可以拆开。

note.en: The first group separates members of the Greek cutting family that look alike. The second holds near-synonyms for study, body and analysis.
note.cn: 第一组区分希腊「切」词族中形近的成员；第二组是表示研究、身体与分析的近义词。

entries.definition: The smallest unit of an element, named by Greek atomos 'uncuttable'. It is the exact opposite prefix to anatomy, which is about cutting up.
entries.definitionCN: 元素的最小单位，名称来自希腊 atomos「不可切的」；它的前缀恰与 anatomy「切开」相反。

entries.definition: Relating to anatomy or to body structure. It modifies nouns such as structure, position and model.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与解剖学或身体结构有关的；修饰 structure、position、model 等名词。

entries.definition: A person who studies or practises anatomy. It names the human agent, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或从事解剖的人；命名的是人，而非领域。

entries.definition: The act of cutting something apart for study. It is the procedure, while anatomy can also be the science or the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究而切开某物的行为；它是操作过程，而 anatomy 还可指学科或结构。

entries.definition: The study of how body parts work. Anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体部件如何运作的学科；anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问它们做什么。

entries.definition: The study of form, especially in biology and linguistics. It is broader than anatomy and does not imply dissection.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形式的学科，尤用于生物学与语言学；比 anatomy 更宽，且不暗示解剖。

entries.definition: The way parts are put together. It is the neutral word; anatomy adds the biological or systematic flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分的组合方式；是中性词，而 anatomy 增添了生物学或系统性的色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ana- 'up, throughout' + temnein 'cut' + -y: the cutting-up that reveals structure.
normal.cn: ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」+ -y：揭示结构的切开。

normal.en: The family runs anatomical, anatomically, anatomist, anatomize, and the -tomy words such as appendectomy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize，以及 appendectomy 一类 -tomy 词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: human anatomy, comparative anatomy, plant anatomy, gross anatomy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：人体解剖学、比较解剖学、植物解剖学、大体解剖学。

normal.en: atom is the same root with the opposite prefix: 'not cuttable' against 'cut up'.
normal.cn: atom 是同一词根加相反前缀：不可切，对比切开。

normal.en: anatomy asks what the parts are; physiology asks what they do.
normal.cn: anatomy 问部件是什么，physiology 问部件做什么。

abstract.en: Picture a watch opened on a table, every wheel laid out in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表在桌上被打开，每个齿轮都按顺序摆好。

abstract.en: Picture a map of a city printed as layers: roads, pipes, then power lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图分层印出：先是道路，再是管道，然后是电线。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence taken apart word by word to see how it holds together.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被逐词拆开，以看清它如何组合。

examples.en: Human anatomy has changed little since the Renaissance.
examples.cn: 自文艺复兴以来，人体解剖学变化不大。

examples.en: The anatomy of a frog is often taught before that of a mammal.
examples.cn: 教学上常先讲青蛙的解剖结构，再讲哺乳动物。

examples.en: Her paper offers an anatomy of the failure rather than a remedy.
examples.cn: 她的论文对这次失败作了剖析，而没有给出补救办法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of cutting: the science, the structure revealed, the cutting itself, metaphorical analysis, the body in speech, plant and animal bodies, institutional structure and the school subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿着「切开」这一动作展开：学科、被揭示的结构、切割本身、比喻性的剖析、口语中的身体、动植物身体、机构结构与学校科目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body opened layer by layer, each part labelled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具被逐层打开、每个部件都带标签的身体。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCIENCE: the physical cutting and the discipline that grew from it.
branches.cn: 动作与学科：实际的切割，以及由它生长出来的学科。

branches.en: WHAT THE CUT REVEALS: human, animal and plant bodies are described part by part.
branches.cn: 切开后所见：人、动物与植物的身体被逐部件描述。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: books, rumours and institutions can be taken apart the same way.
branches.cn: 比喻延伸：书籍、谣言与机构也能以同样方式拆解。

branches.en: THE BODY IN SPEECH: informal use lets the noun stand for the whole body.
branches.cn: 口语中的身体：非正式用法让该名词代指整个身体。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: in medical schools the science becomes a course with examinations.
branches.cn: 科目：在医学院，这门科学变成有考试的课程。

intro.en: Anatomy is a Greek compound: a prefix of opening, the verb 'to cut', and a noun ending. English also uses the combining form -tomy for surgical cuttings.
intro.cn: anatomy 是希腊语复合词：表示打开的动词前缀、动词「切」，以及名词词尾。英语还用构词成分 -tomy 表示外科切开。

latinIntro.en: Latin anatomia came from Greek anatomē. The Latinized form supplies anatomy, anatomical, anatomist and anatomize; the Greek root tom- supplies appendectomy, tonsillectomy and lobotomy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 来自希腊 anatomē；拉丁化形式衍生 anatomy、anatomical、anatomist、anatomize；希腊词根 tom- 衍生 appendectomy、tonsillectomy、lobotomy。

senses.title: Of the Science
senses.titleCN: 解剖学的：属于这门学科
senses.definition: belonging to the science of anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 属于解剖学这门学科的
senses.example: The anatomical literature on the wrist is enormous.
senses.exampleCN: 关于腕部的解剖学文献浩如烟海。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the noun to the discipline. In this sense it sits beside histological, physiological and embryological as labels of research fields.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词挂到学科上；在这一义项里，它与 histological、physiological、embryological 并列，都是研究领域的标签。

senses.title: Of Body Structure
senses.titleCN: 身体结构的：讲部件怎么长
senses.definition: relating to the actual structure of a body
senses.definitionCN: 与身体实际结构有关的
senses.example: The anatomical difference between the two species is small.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种在身体结构上的差异很小。
senses.why: Here the reference is to parts and their arrangement, not to books about them. A difference is anatomical when it lies in structure rather than in behaviour or chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 这里指的是部件及其排列，而不是关于它们的书籍。当差异存在于结构而非行为或化学时，就说它是 anatomical 的差异。

senses.title: Structural, by Metaphor
senses.titleCN: 结构上的：用于非生物对象
senses.definition: relating to the internal structure of a non-biological thing
senses.definitionCN: 与非生物事物的内部结构有关
senses.example: The anatomical weaknesses of the treaty were obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约在结构上的弱点显而易见。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an institution as a body with joints. It is looser than the biological sense and often signals that a failure lies in design, not in execution.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把机构当作有骨架的身体；它比生物学义更宽松，常暗示问题出在设计而非执行。

senses.title: For Display or Study
senses.definition: made to show or study body structure
senses.definitionCN: 为展示或研究身体结构而制作的
senses.example: The anatomical model comes apart in twelve layers, from skin to bone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个解剖模型可以拆成十二层，从皮肤到骨骼。
senses.why: Objects as well as ideas can be anatomical: a model, a chart, a plate. The word then labels the purpose of the object, not a branch of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 物体也能是 anatomical 的：模型、挂图、图版。此时这个词标出的是该物件的用途，而不是知识分支。

senses.title: Standard Reference Position
senses.titleCN: 解剖学姿势的：标准化方位
senses.definition: relating to the standard position used to describe body parts
senses.definitionCN: 与描述身体部件时所用的标准姿势有关
senses.example: In the anatomical position the palms face forward.
senses.exampleCN: 在解剖学姿势中，手掌朝前。
senses.why: Description needs a fixed frame, or 'left' and 'right' mean nothing. The adjective marks that frame, which is a convention rather than a fact of the body.
senses.whyCN: 描述需要一个固定参照，否则「左」「右」毫无意义；这个形容词标出的正是那一参照，它是约定而非身体的事实。

senses.title: Recognizable in Structure
senses.titleCN: 解剖上可辨识的：结构上找得到
senses.definition: identifiable by its structure when examined
senses.definitionCN: 检查时能凭结构辨认出来的
senses.example: The tumour was anatomically distinct from the surrounding tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 该肿瘤在结构上与周围组织明显不同。
senses.why: Surgeons and radiologists ask whether a thing can be told apart by its parts. Anatomically distinct means the difference is visible in structure, before any chemical test.
senses.whyCN: 外科医生与放射科医生要问：某物能否凭其部件被区分开来。anatomically distinct 意为差异在结构上就可见，无需等到化学检验。

senses.title: Of the Anatomy Course
senses.definition: belonging to the teaching of anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 属于解剖学教学的
senses.example: The anatomical drawings were hung in the dissection room.
senses.exampleCN: 解剖图挂在解剖室里。
senses.why: Teaching produces its own vocabulary and objects. In this sense the adjective points to the classroom and its materials rather than to research.
senses.whyCN: 教学会产出自己的词汇与物件；在这一义项里，这个形容词指向课堂及其教材，而不是科研。

senses.title: Analytic, Part by Part
senses.titleCN: 结构分析的：逐部件拆解
senses.definition: treating a subject by separating its parts
senses.definitionCN: 把对象按部件分开处理
senses.example: The critic offered an anatomical reading of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这位批评家对小说作了结构解剖式的解读。
senses.why: This is the adjective of the metaphorical noun: an analysis that names each part and its function. It is more formal than 'structural' and more vivid than 'detailed'.
senses.whyCN: 这是比喻义名词的形容词形式：一种逐一点明每个部件及其作用的分析。它比 structural 更正式，比 detailed 更生动。

intro.en: Anatomical is anatomy plus -ical. Anatomy comes from Greek anatomē 'a cutting up', from ana- 'up, throughout' and temnein 'to cut'. The English adjective is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: anatomical 是 anatomy 加 -ical。anatomy 出自希腊 anatomē「切开」，由 ana-「向上、遍及」与 temnein「切」构成。英语形容词的年代仅为约数。

items.en: Temnein 'to cut' gave the noun tomos 'a cut piece' and the suffix -tomos. English keeps that suffix in surgical names such as appendectomy and lobotomy.
items.cn: temnein「切」给出名词 tomos「切下的一片」与后缀 -tomos；英语在外科名称中保留该后缀，如 appendectomy、lobotomy。

items.en: Anatomē meant the act of cutting up a body. Greek medicine used the word for dissection, and the study of parts grew around that practice.
items.cn: anatomē 指把身体切开的动作；希腊医学用这个词表示解剖，而关于部件的研究正是围绕这一实践发展起来的。

items.en: Latin anatomia carried both the procedure and the knowledge gained. Medieval Latin writers also used it for a written summary of body parts.
items.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 兼指操作过程与所获知识；中世纪拉丁作者也用它指关于身体部件的书面概述。

items.en: English anatomy appears in the sixteenth century, and the adjective anatomical followed in the same period or shortly after. The exact first citation of the adjective is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 anatomy 于十六世纪出现，形容词 anatomical 在同一时期或稍后跟上。该形容词的确切首见书证不确定。

items.en: Medicine fixed phrases such as anatomical position, anatomical variation and gross anatomical features. Each borrows the adjective to mark a standard frame or a level of observation.
items.cn: 医学固定了 anatomical position（解剖学姿势）、anatomical variation（解剖变异）、gross anatomical features（大体解剖特征）等说法；每个都借这个形容词标出标准参照或观察层次。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from its noun and from its adverb. The second holds near-synonyms that describe structure at different levels.
note.cn: 第一组区分该形容词与其名词、副词；第二组是描述不同层次结构的近义词。

entries.definition: The field, the structure or the act of dissection. It is what the adjective describes, so the two never occupy the same slot in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指学科、结构或解剖行为；它是该形容词所描述的对象，因此两者在句中不会占据同一位置。

entries.definition: Means 'in terms of body structure'. It modifies verbs and adjectives, as in anatomically correct or anatomically distinct.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「在身体结构方面」；修饰动词与形容词，如 anatomically correct、anatomically distinct。

entries.definition: A person who studies anatomy. It never replaces the adjective before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指研究解剖学的人；它不能替代名词前的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to structure of any kind, biological or not. It is the broader and safer word where no body is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何结构有关，无论是否生物；在不涉及身体时，它更宽泛也更稳妥。

entries.definition: Relating to form and shape, especially in biology and linguistics. It stresses outward form rather than internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 与形式和外形有关，尤用于生物学与语言学；强调外部形态，而非内部排列。

entries.definition: Relating to the microscopic study of tissues. It is a level below gross anatomy, so it is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织的显微研究有关；它比大体解剖低一个层次，因此并非同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to how the body works. It contrasts with anatomical, which concerns what the parts are and where they sit.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体如何运作有关；它与 anatomical 相对，后者关心部件是什么、位于何处。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: anatomy + -ical: belonging to the cutting-up science or to the structure it reveals.
normal.cn: anatomy + -ical：属于「切开之学」，或属于它揭示的结构。

normal.en: The family runs anatomy, anatomical, anatomically, anatomist, anatomize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 anatomy、anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: anatomical structure, anatomical position, anatomical model, anatomical variation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：解剖结构、解剖学姿势、解剖模型、解剖变异。

normal.en: anatomical is about parts; physiological is about functions.
normal.cn: anatomical 讲部件，physiological 讲功能。

normal.en: atom carries the same root with a negative prefix: not cuttable, against cut up.
normal.cn: atom 是同一词根加否定前缀：不可切，与切开相对。

abstract.en: Picture a numbered diagram where every line points to one small part.
abstract.cn: 想象一张编号示意图，每条引线都指向一个小部件。

abstract.en: Picture a machine manual that begins by naming every screw before explaining what it does.
abstract.cn: 想象一本机器手册，先给每颗螺丝命名，再解释它的作用。

abstract.en: Picture two animals that look alike until you compare their skeletons.
abstract.cn: 想象两只动物外表相似，直到比较骨架才发现不同。

examples.en: The two species differ in anatomical detail but not in behaviour.
examples.cn: 这两个物种在解剖细节上不同，行为上却没有差别。

examples.en: The surgeon studied the anatomical charts before the operation.
examples.cn: 手术前外科医生仔细看了解剖图。

examples.en: An anatomically modern skeleton was found in the cave.
examples.cn: 洞穴中发现了一具结构上属于现代人的骨架。

dict_mnemonic.text: anatomy（解剖）+ ical（……的）→ 解剖学的、身体结构的

root: 希腊 ana-「向上、遍及」+ temnein「切」→ anatomē「切开」→ 拉丁 anatomia → 英语 anatomy → anatomical。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses attach the adjective to different things: a science, a body's parts, a non-biological structure, a teaching model, a standard position, a visible difference, a course and a method of analysis.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个形容词挂到不同对象上：一门学科、身体的部件、非生物结构、教学模型、标准姿势、可见差异、课程与分析方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled chart where every line points to one part of a body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张带标签的图，每条引线都指向身体的一个部件。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS TEACHING: the adjective marks research literature and classroom materials alike.
branches.cn: 学科及其教学：这个形容词既可标出研究文献，也可标出课堂教材。

branches.en: STRUCTURE MADE VISIBLE: parts and their arrangement, including differences that can be seen before any test.
branches.cn: 可见的结构：部件及其排列，包括无需检验就能看出的差异。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: institutions and texts can be treated as bodies to be taken apart.
branches.cn: 比喻：机构与文本都可被当作身体来拆解。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a model or chart is anatomical because of the use it serves.
branches.cn: 物件：模型或挂图之所以是 anatomical 的，是因为它服务的用途。

branches.en: THE CONVENTION: a standard position makes left and right describable at all.
branches.cn: 约定：标准姿势才使「左」「右」变得可以描述。

intro.en: Anatomical is a Greek compound with an English adjective ending: a prefix of opening, the verb 'to cut', the noun -y, and the adjective suffix -ical.
intro.cn: anatomical 是希腊复合词加英语形容词词尾：表示打开的前缀、动词「切」、名词词尾 -y，以及形容词后缀 -ical。

latinIntro.en: Latin anatomia supplies anatomy, anatomical, anatomically, anatomist and anatomize. The Greek root tom- also yields atom, tome, epitome and the surgical -ectomy names.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 anatomia 衍生 anatomy、anatomical、anatomically、anatomist、anatomize；希腊词根 tom- 还给出 atom、tome、epitome 以及外科的 -ectomy 类名称。

items.meaning: of body structure or of anatomy
items.example: The anatomical atlas has forty plates.
items.exampleCN: 这本解剖图谱有四十幅图版。

items.example: Anatomy was taught with drawings before it was taught with bodies.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学先以图画教授，后来才用实体。

items.example: The two hands are anatomically symmetrical.
items.exampleCN: 两只手在结构上是对称的。

items.example: The anatomist corrected the older drawing.
items.exampleCN: 这位解剖学家修正了那幅旧图。

items.example: She anatomized the contract clause by clause.
items.exampleCN: 她把合同逐条剖析了一遍。

items.example: The word atom once meant 'uncuttable'.
items.exampleCN: atom 一词原意是「不可切的」。

items.example: A single tome filled the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 一卷书就占满了书架。

items.meaning: a cutting short; a perfect example
items.example: The village is the epitome of calm.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄是宁静的典型。

definition_zh: 目标；目的；球门；进球得分；终点
definition_en: the end point you aim at, whether a line to cross, a result to achieve, or a frame to put the ball into
core_image: 跑道尽头插着的一面旗，所有脚步都朝它收拢
scene: 决赛的最后时刻，前锋一脚把球踢进了球门。 She scored the winning goal in the last minute of the match.
sceneCN: 这里 goal 是「进球、得分」（第 4 个义项：把球送进球门所得到的一分）；句意：她在比赛最后一分钟打入了制胜的一球。场景要点：球门网、飞过门线的球、停在最后一分钟的计时器，以及看台上举起的手臂。

pos.zh: 目标；目的；终点
（体育）球门；进球得分

守门员
球门柱

senses.title: The end point of a race
senses.definition: the mark or line at which a race ends
senses.definitionCN: 赛跑结束处的标记或界线
senses.example: The runners sprinted toward the goal at the far end of the track.
senses.exampleCN: 选手们朝跑道尽头的终点冲刺。
senses.why: Goal is first recorded in the 1530s as the end point of a race. The word names the mark that ends motion, and its own origin is not settled.
senses.whyCN: goal 最早在 16 世纪 30 年代记录为赛跑的终点。这个词命名的是让运动结束的那个标记，而它自身的来源尚无定论。

senses.title: The object of an effort
senses.definition: the result or state that a person or group works toward
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体努力要达成的结果或状态
senses.example: Her goal is to finish the marathon under four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她的目标是在四小时内跑完马拉松。
senses.why: The figurative sense, also from the 1540s, treats life as a course: the result you want is the mark you run toward.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻义同样始于 16 世纪 40 年代：它把人生当作一段赛程，你想要的结果就是你朝它奔跑的那个标记。

senses.title: The frame where the ball is put
senses.definition: the structure of posts and net into which players try to send the ball
senses.definitionCN: 由门柱和球网构成、球员努力把球送进去的结构
senses.example: The goalkeeper stood between the posts of the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员站在球门柱之间。
senses.why: The sports sense, also from the 1540s, makes the end point physical: a frame marks the place where the ball must arrive.
senses.whyCN: 同样始于 16 世纪 40 年代的体育义项，把终点变成实物：一个框架标出了球必须抵达的位置。

senses.title: A score made in the frame
senses.definition: a point gained by sending the ball through or into the goal
senses.definitionCN: 把球送过门线或送进球门而得到的一分
senses.example: She scored the winning goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一分钟打入了制胜的一球。
senses.why: By metonymy the frame gives its name to the event of putting the ball through it: the endpoint becomes the point gained.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，框架把自己的名字借给了“把球送进去”这件事：终点变成了所得的一分。

senses.title: A measured target in work
senses.definition: a figure or quota that a team or company is expected to reach
senses.definitionCN: 团队或公司被要求达到的数字或定额
senses.example: The sales team missed its quarterly goal by two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 销售团队以两个百分点的差距未能达到季度指标。
senses.why: A number can serve as the mark: once the target is measurable, the race endpoint becomes a quota.
senses.whyCN: 数字也可以充当那个标记：一旦目标可以计量，赛跑的终点就变成了定额。

senses.title: A long-term aim in life
senses.definition: a distant aim that gives direction to a person's life or career
senses.definitionCN: 为人生或事业提供方向的远期追求
senses.example: His goal is to run a clinic in his home town.
senses.exampleCN: 他的志向是在家乡开一家诊所。
senses.why: The largest version of the same image: a whole life is the course, and one distant mark gives it direction.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一个意象的最大版本：整个人生是赛程，一个远处的标记为它提供方向。

senses.title: Own goal: a score against your own side
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase own goal, a goal scored accidentally for the opposing team
senses.definitionCN: 在固定搭配 own goal 中，指误为对方球队打进的一球
senses.example: The defender's own goal decided the tie.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫的乌龙球决定了这场平局的结果。
senses.why: The frame is neutral: a ball put into the wrong one still counts. English names that accident with the fixed phrase own goal.
senses.whyCN: 球门本身是中立的：球进了错误的那一个，仍然算数。英语用固定说法 own goal 命名这种意外。

senses.title: Goal line and goal area
senses.definition: the line and the marked area on the field that belong to the goal
senses.definitionCN: 场地上属于球门的那条线和被划出的区域
senses.example: The ball crossed the goal line by a few centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 球越过球门线几厘米。
senses.why: The frame projects a boundary onto the field; the line and the area are the ground version of the same endpoint.
senses.whyCN: 球门把一条边界投射到场地上；球门线与球门区是同一个终点在地面上的版本。

senses.title: Attributive: goal-directed, goal-setting
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe activity organised around a target
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词之前，描述围绕目标组织起来的活动
senses.example: Goal-setting theory treats clear targets as a motivator.
senses.exampleCN: 目标设定理论把清晰的目标视为一种激励因素。
senses.why: When the word moves in front of another noun, it stops naming a mark and starts labelling the activity that is organised around one.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词移到另一个名词前面时，它不再命名一个标记，而是给围绕某个标记组织起来的活动贴标签。

intro.en: Goal is a single noun of uncertain origin: it appears in the 1530s as the end of a race, and every later sense keeps that 'mark ahead' shape.
intro.cn: goal 是一个来源不确定的单词：它在 16 世纪 30 年代以“赛跑终点”出现，后来每个义项都保留着“前方有一个标记”的形状。

items.en: First recorded as 'end point of a race'. The word appears once earlier, as gol in an early-14c poem, with an apparent sense of 'boundary, limit'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“赛跑的终点”。这个词更早还出现过一次，在 14 世纪早期的一首诗里写作 gol，似乎是“边界、界限”的意思。

items.en: Three origins have been proposed and none is established: Old English *gal 'obstacle, barrier', implied by gælan 'to hinder' and by compounds such as singal and widgal; Old Norse geil 'a narrow glen, a passage'; or Old French gaule 'long pole, stake', which is Germanic in origin. The source is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 先后有三种来源被提出，但没有一种得到确认：一是古英语 *gal“障碍、壁垒”，由 gælan“阻碍”以及 singal、widgal 等复合词推知；二是古诺尔斯语 geil“狭窄峡谷、通道”；三是古法语 gaule“长杆、桩”，而后者本身出自日耳曼语。词源属于存疑。

items.en: The sports sense 'place where the ball is put to score' is recorded, and in the same decade the figurative sense 'object of an effort'.
items.cn: 记录到体育义“把球放进去得分的位置”，同一时期还出现比喻义“努力的目标”。

items.en: Goal-keeper appears in the 1650s; field goal in 1889; goal-tender in 1889; goalie in 1921 as a shortening of goal-tender.
items.cn: goal-keeper 出现于 17 世纪 50 年代；field goal 与 goal-tender 出现于 1889 年；goalie 于 1921 年作为 goal-tender 的缩略形式出现。

items.en: Goalpost, goal line, goal area, own goal and goalless fill out the family. Goal itself remains a noun only; there is no verb 'to goal' in standard English.
items.cn: goalpost、goal line、goal area、own goal、goalless 补全了这一词族。goal 本身始终只是名词；标准英语中没有 to goal 这样的动词用法。

items.en: Gold is a different word with a different history; the resemblance to goal is only in sound and spelling. German Ziel means 'goal, target' but is not the source of the English word.
items.cn: gold 是另一个词，来历完全不同；它与 goal 的相似只在读音和拼写上。德语 Ziel 意为“目标、终点”，但它并不是英语这个词的来源。

note.en: The first group is sound and spelling neighbours, including two that merely look like goal; the second compares the words for what you are trying to reach.
note.cn: 第一组是读音与拼写上的邻居，其中两个只是看起来像 goal；第二组比较表示“你想要抵达的东西”的几个词。

entries.definition: the yellow metal. It has no historical link with goal; only the vowel and the final consonant resemble each other.
entries.definitionCN: 那种黄色金属。它与 goal 没有任何历史联系，只是元音和结尾辅音相近。

entries.definition: one of the two uprights of a goal. It is a compound of goal plus post, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 球门两根立柱之一。它是 goal 加 post 的合成词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a goalkeeper. It is a 1921 shortening of goal-tender, so it belongs to the goal family.
entries.definitionCN: 守门员。它是 1921 年对 goal-tender 的缩略，因此属于 goal 词族。

entries.definition: without a goal being scored, as in a goalless draw. The suffix -less marks absence, not a new sense.
entries.definitionCN: 没有进球的，如 goalless draw。后缀 -less 标记“没有”，并不产生新义项。

entries.definition: what you intend to achieve; also the act of pointing at something. It is close to goal but often more personal and less measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 你打算达成的东西；也指瞄准的动作。它与 goal 接近，但往往更个人化、更不可量化。

entries.definition: a specific result that an organisation formally sets out to achieve. It is more formal and more measurable than goal.
entries.definitionCN: 组织正式设定要达成的具体结果。它比 goal 更正式、更可量化。

entries.definition: a level or figure to be reached, often with a deadline. It stresses the number to hit, while goal stresses the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 需要达到的水平或数字，常带截止时间。它强调要命中的数字，而 goal 强调方向。

entries.definition: the reason something exists or is done. It answers 'why', while goal answers 'where to'.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在或被做的理由。它回答“为什么”，而 goal 回答“往哪里去”。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts and real relatives: the noun goal, its compounds goalpost and goalkeeper, and the 1921 shortening goalie.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构词成分与真实同族词：名词 goal，它的合成词 goalpost、goalkeeper，以及 1921 年的缩略形式 goalie。

normal.en: Goal first meant the end of a race: a mark you run toward.
normal.cn: goal 最初指赛跑的终点：一个你朝它奔跑的标记。

normal.en: The sports frame is that same mark made visible, and the score is named after the frame.
normal.cn: 体育中的球门就是同一个标记变成实物，而“得分”又被球门命名。

normal.en: Gold and goal are only neighbours in sound; they have no shared history.
normal.cn: gold 与 goal 只是读音上的邻居，没有共同的来历。

normal.en: Own goal is a fixed phrase: the ball goes into the frame, but the wrong one.
normal.cn: own goal 是固定说法：球确实进了门，只是进错了那一个。

normal.en: Goal-setting and goal-directed show the noun working as a modifier, common in psychology and management.
normal.cn: goal-setting 与 goal-directed 显示这个名词可以作修饰语，这在心理学与管理学中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture a flag at the end of a track: every lane converges on it.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道尽头插着一面旗：每一条跑道都朝它收拢。

abstract.en: The flag can be a line, a number, a frame or a distant plan; the word always points to one mark.
abstract.cn: 那面旗可以是一条线、一个数字、一个框架，或一个远期的计划；这个词始终指向同一个标记。

abstract.en: A goal is not the running; it is the place where the running stops being open.
abstract.cn: 目标不是奔跑本身；它是奔跑不再敞开的那一点。

examples.en: The team's goal is to cut water use by a third within five years.
examples.cn: 这个团队的目标是在五年内把用水量削减三分之一。

examples.en: He scored twice and set up the third goal.
examples.cn: 他打进两球，并助攻了第三个进球。

examples.en: Without a clear goal, the meetings drifted from topic to topic.
examples.cn: 没有明确的目标，会议就从一个话题漂到另一个话题。

root: 词源存疑：最早指赛跑的终点（1530 年代），可能来自古英语表示“障碍、界限”的词或古法语“长杆”；核心是“所有努力都朝向的那个终点”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of goal, all built on one position: a mark placed ahead, which motion or effort is organised to reach.
sensesIntro.cn: goal 的九个义项都建立在同一个位置关系上：前方放着一个标记，运动或努力都围绕抵达它来组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark ahead that every step converges on.
core.cn: 核心意象：前方的一个标记，所有脚步都朝它收拢。

branches.en: RACE: the original sense is the physical end point of a course.
branches.cn: 赛跑：最初的义项就是赛程的物理终点。

branches.en: AIM: the mark becomes mental, from a single task to a whole life's direction.
branches.cn: 目标：标记变成心里的，从一项任务一直到整个人生的方向。

branches.en: FRAME: in sport the mark is built of posts and line, a place the ball must reach.
branches.cn: 球门：在体育中，标记由门柱与门线构成，是球必须抵达的位置。

branches.en: SCORE: the frame lends its name to the point, including the accidental own goal.
branches.cn: 得分：球门把名字借给那一分，也包括意外的乌龙球。

branches.en: MEASURE: a number can be the mark, and the noun can label activity organised around it.
branches.cn: 计量：数字可以成为标记，这个名词也能给围绕标记组织的活动贴标签。

intro.en: Goal is not built from prefixes or suffixes; it is one noun whose family is made of compounds and a few endings such as -ie, -less and the plural -s.
intro.cn: goal 不是由前缀或后缀构成的；它是一个单词名词，其词族由合成词和 -ie、-less、复数 -s 等少数词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is known. The word appears in English in the 1530s with an uncertain origin, and the three candidates are Old English, Old Norse and Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 没有已知的拉丁语来源。这个词在 16 世纪 30 年代出现于英语，来源不确定，三个候选分别来自古英语、古诺尔斯语与古法语。

intro.en: Elite is Old French eslite, the chosen ones, from eslire, which goes back to Latin eligere, to pick out; the elite are simply those picked out of the rest.
intro.cn: elite 是古法语 eslite（被选中的人），来自 eslire，可上溯到拉丁语 eligere（挑出来）；精英就是从其余人里被挑出来的那批。

items.en: Latin legere means to gather or choose.
items.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为收集或挑选。

items.en: Adding ex- gives eligere, to pick out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 eligere，意为挑出来。

items.en: Old French eslite, from eslire, meant the chosen ones.
items.cn: 古法语 eslite 来自 eslire，意为被选中的人。

items.en: English took elite in the 18C for the best or the powerful few.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪借用 elite，指最优秀者或少数权贵。

items.en: Writers used elite for a social class set above the rest.
items.cn: 作家用 elite 指高于其余人的社会阶层。

items.en: Sport and education made elite a label for the top level.

note.en: Elite and elect share the Latin root for choosing; elite names the chosen few, while elitism turns that into a doctrine about who should lead.

dict_mnemonic.text: elite 来自古法语 eslite「被选中的人」，词根是拉丁 eligere（e- 外 ＋ legere 挑）＝挑出来。所以 elite 的本义就是「被挑出来的那一批」：the elite 精英（集合名词，谓语可用复数），elite athletes 顶尖运动员，elite forces 精锐部队，the ruling elite 统治精英。加后缀派生：-ism → elitism 精英主义（认为该由少数优秀者领导），-ist → elitist 精英主义者（常带贬义）。同根词 elect 选举、select 挑选、eligible 符合条件的。近义 aristocracy 靠出身的贵族，vanguard 走在最前面的先锋，the cream of the crop 一批里最好的部分。注意 elite 作形容词时没有 -er/-est，比较级用 more elite。
